Shanghai City-Bus
 More than 10 Shanghai bus companies operate about 1,600 city bus lines in downtown and suburbs, offering convenient alternatives to metro. These lines can be identified either by numbers or Chinese characters representing the terminals. Shanghai bus stops of most downtown lines are announced by automatic reporter in Mandarin, Shanghai dialect and English, while a small part are announced in Mandarin and Shanghai dialect only.
Shanghai City Bus Routes
1. Regular Downtown Lines: 1 to 992, Daqiao Line 3 to 6, Tunnel Line 1, 2, 3, 6 & 8
2. District/Regional Lines & Suburban Lines: Starting with Pudong, Jiading, Baoshan, Qingpu, Minhang, Fengxian, Songjiang…
 City Bus Terminal Station 
3. Cross-district Lines: Starting with Huzhu Express, Shangzhu, Shangshi, Nanchuan, Xinjia, Songmei, Songxin, Shenchong, Lianzhu, Nanqing, Huqingying…
4. Night Lines: 301 to 345, Xumin Special Line, Tunnel Night Line 1
5. Downtown Shuttle Bus: 1001 to 1849 to solve the last-kilometer commute to/from metro station, and transfer between main roads and communities.
6. Rush-hour Lines: 04 -1090, Songjiang Line 29, Daqiao Line 1, Lingang No.2, Qinghua Special Line, Singjiang No.29
7. Sightseeing Bus: City Sightseeing Lines by Spring Tour, Shanghai Bus Tours, Shencheng Sightseeing Bus …
8. Shanghai airport to city bus: Pudong Airport Shuttle Bus, Hongqiao Airport Shuttle Bus
9. Other categories: Hongqiao Transport Hub Line 1 & 4 to 10, Ferry Lines, Customized Line, BRT Nantuan Line, BRT Fengpu Line
10. Intercity Lines: K319 & routes starting with Bahe, Huliu, Taijia, Jiashan, Kunshan, Pinghu, Yangshan and Qingshang.  
Shanghai Bus Schedule
 Most bus routes start running from 05:30 – 06:30 and stop service at 19:30 – 21:30.
 Rush-hour Lines operate from 06:00 – 08:00 to 16:30 – 18:30.
 Night Lines are in operation from 23:00 to 05:30 the next day. 
Shanghai Bus Fare & How to Pay
The city bus fare varies a little according to the vehicle types. Most routes including the downtown lines, suburban lines, night lines and rush-hour lines charge CNY2. The downtown shuttle buses only cost CNY1.
Passengers need to prepare some loose change to insert coins or banknotes into the coin box, or swipe the Shanghai Public Transportation Card to pay.
Most cross-district lines charge by distance and the ticket price is CNY1-12. Conductors sell tickets on these city buses on which passengers must pay in cash. Getting on the Bus Inside a city bus  
Shanghai Sightseeing Bus
Tourists can have a general look at Puxi, Pudong by the double-decked City Sightseeing Lines 1, 2, 3 & 5. They can hop on and hop off to visit attractions including Nanjing Road, the Bund, People's Square, Yu Garden, Xintiandi and Shanghai Museum. There are also three lines of Big Bus Tours connecting must-gos in Shanghai.
Shanghai Tourist Bus
Shanghai direct tourist buses set off at the airport and popular sites in the city center, taking tourists to Wuzhen, West Lake, Lion Grove Garden, Humble Administrator’s Garden ...

Trams in Shanghai
Songjiang Tram Lines:Line T1 connects Canghua Road and Xinqiao, while line T2 is a loop line running around Songjiang University Town. Songjiang Tram Line T3 to T6 is under construction. Shanghai will have more tram lines in Fengxian District and Pudong New Area in the future.

Huangpu District, Shanghai
Huangpu District Facts
Chinese Name: 黄浦区 (huáng pǔ qū)
Population: 852,476
Area: 20.5 square kilometers (7.92 square miles)
Location: in the center of Shanghai, east China
Area Code: 021
Zip Code: 200001
GDP (2018): CNY2,270.31 billion (USD 343.10 billion)
Traditional City Center
Huangpu District, subordinate to Shanghai, is located in the southwest end of the confluence of Huangpu River and Suzhou River. It is close to Hongkou District and Yangpu District on the north, Luwan District on the south, Jing’an District on the west, and Pudong New Area on the east. It is one of the most prosperous and central areas of Shanghai where visitors can appreciate the wonderful cityscape. In addition, there are many Shanghai landmarks, old buildings and streets such as the Bund, Shanghai People's Square, Nanjing Road, Yu Garden and Shanghai Museum. It is better to spend 2-3 days to have an enjoyable Huangpu District travel.
Best Places to Visit & Top Things to Do in Huangpu District
 The Bund
Near to Huangpu River, the Bund is one of the must-see scenic spots in Huangpu District Shanghai with 33 buildings in different styles. Numerous skyscrapers that stand on the opposite side of the Huangpu River can be seen in the Bund, such as the Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower and  World Financial Center. At night, visitors can take a Huangpu River cruise at the Bund to enjoy the stunning night scenery.
 Nanjing Road
Nanjing Road is one of the ten famous pedestrian streets in China and the earliest commercial street established after the opening of Shanghai port. It is a shopping paradise as a lot of department stores gather here with a complete range of goods. Creative city sculptures are everywhere, and there are plenty of chairs in the middle of the street for visitors to relax. It's a good experience to ride a scaled-down version of the old tram which was the main transportation method in Shanghai before.
 Yu Garden
Built in the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644), Yu Garden is known as one of the five classical gardens in Shanghai with the exquisite pavilions, halls, rockeries, ponds and cloisters. The highlights of Yu Garden include the Great Rockery, Cuixiu Hall, Sansui Hall, Wanhua Chamber and Exquisite Jade Rock. On the outside of Yu Garden is Yuyuan Bazaar where visitors can buy souvenirs and taste delicious foods.
 Shanghai Museum
Shanghai Museum is a large museum of ancient Chinese art, with 12 special exhibition rooms and over 120,000 fine collections. The museum gathers historical relics of different dynasties, especially bronzes, chinaware, calligraphy and paintings. In addition, special exhibitions are often held in the museum, displaying various Chinese and foreign cultural relics, art works, calligraphy and paintings.
Best Time to Visit Huangpu District
The best time to visit Huangpu District Shanghai is March to May and October to November when the climate is relatively pleasant with the average temperature of 15℃ (59℉). Huangpu District China has four distinctive seasons. From July to August are the hottest months of the year and the highest temperature is 37℃ (97℉). December to February is the coldest period of the year with a temperature of 7℃ (45℉). The rainy season in Shanghai starts in the middle of June every year and lasts for a month. It is not a good time to have a Shanghai travel.

Transportation
Visitors can fly to Shanghai Pudong International Airport and then take Metro Line 2 to Huangpu District Shanghai or to Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport and then take Metro Line 10 to there. It is easy to reach there by bullet trains as the Shanghai Railway Station provides all kinds of scheduled trains.
Metro, buses and taxis are the main transportation means in Huangpu District Shanghai. The Shanghai Maglev Train also serves the public and visitors can reach the Shanghai Pudong International Airport in 40 minutes. Metro Line 1, 2, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 13 are available there. Visitors can take Metro Line 10 and 2 to get to the Bund and Nanjing Road. It is also recommended to take the Shanghai Sightseeing Bus for a one-day or two-day city tour. The starting price and charging standard of Shanghai taxi are different between day and night.
 See more: Shanghai Metro
Best Huangpu Food to Try
The best Huangpu District Shanghai foods to try are Steamed Buns, Pan Fried Pork Bun, Sweet Soup Balls, Ribs Rice Cakes and Shanghai Cuisine. And visitors can taste many local dishes or snacks in Yunnan South Road.
Shanghai Cuisine: It is characterized by using much oil and soy sauce to make moderate, original and mellow flavors. The popular dishes include Yan Du Xian Soup, Stewed Pork with Brown Sauce, Fried Prawns and Eight-treasure Delicious Duck.

Shanghai Weather in February
 Shanghai suffers from damp and relatively cold air in February. Rainy days account for more than 10 days on average, but the good news is that there are rarely heavy or long-term rains. As long as you can endure a little low temperature, you can have a relatively good tour in February, when Shanghai is surrounded by decorations for the Chinese New Year and flowers like plum blossoms.
TemperatureAs a winter month in Shanghai, February features relatively cold weather. On most days, the daytime has a temperature range of 6-15 degrees Celsius (43-59 degrees Fahrenheit), and the nighttime experiences a colder climate with the temperature of 0-10°C (32-50°F).  Cold February 
The temperature in February is somewhat unstable. The first half of the month may have very cold days, though in rare instances, with daily highs dipping below 5°C (41°F) and lows potentially falling below 0°C (32°F). Conversely, the latter half of the month occasionally sees quite warm days with daily highs exceeding 20°C (68°F).
All in all, you are recommended to pay attention to the weather forecast and bring enough clothes to deal with the temperature fluctuations.
Apparent Temperature May Be Lower.Sometimes, the apparent temperature is much lower than the weather forecast tells. On the one hand, the humidity is relatively high and averages at around 71%. As a result, the air feels uncomfortably clammy and colder. On the other hand, winds sweep Shanghai occasionally in February, which tend to be stronger in riverside areas like the Bund, making the apparent temperature 3-5°C (5-9°F) lower.
PrecipitationThere are about 12 rainy days on average in Shanghai in February. However, you should not be discouraged by this number. Actually, the monthly precipitation averages only 60 mm, and the rain is usually light or lasts for a short period, meaning that it won’t influence your trip a lot. Sleet may fall this month, but only with a small chance. 
Days with or after precipitation are usually colder, so wear more if you go out for a visit on those days. Colder Rainy Days of Shanghai in February  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursDaylight hours are in an increasing trend in February, but relatively short: they are about 10.4 hours and 11.3 hours, respectively, at the beginning and the end of the month. Since the sun sets quite early at around 17:29-17:52, getting up early is advised if you want to have a rich trip. Alternatively, you can extend your time on the daily tour by arranging some night visits. Anyway, the night views of Shanghai are awesome and the Bund is always on the top list. 
Generally, rainy and overcast moments occupy many hours of the daytime, and the sunshine hours are only 4 on average per day. The good news is that the sunshine is soft at this time, and you can enjoy outings without any sun-protection measures.

What to Wear in Shanghai in February? Tops: Given the changeable climate of Shanghai in February, clothes of various thicknesses are needed. In detail, you are recommended to bring long-sleeved T-shirts and shirts; hoodies and knitwear; thick jackets like padded leather jackets and wool coats; and thin down jackets. 
On most daytime hours, long-sleeved shirts, hoodies, plus padded leather jackets; or long-sleeved T-shirts, knitwear, plus wool coats are suitable and comfortable to wear. During the daytime hours on some quite warm days, the outermost layer may need to be taken off. Then, during the nighttime hours, down jackets are generally necessary.
Bottoms: For pants, thick jeans and sweatpants are both suitable choices. Long johns are useful for activities like taking the Huangpu River cruise at night. The shoes you bring should be warm and comfortable for walking, so you can bring various thick flats and sneakers. 
Others: Always take rain gear with you in case it rains. Hats and scarves are better to be packed.
What Is Shanghai Like in February?
In 2027, both the Chinese New Year and the Lantern Festival will fall in February. At this time, Shanghai finds itself enveloped in the lively festive atmosphere. In addition, some flowers begin to bloom. 
1. Yu Garden
Within the classical Garden, flowers like daffodils and plum blossoms compete to bloom. Outside the Garden, numerous large-scale lanterns themed around the Chinese New Year are visible. During the Lantern Festival period, activities like lantern riddle guessing and folk performances will enrich your itinerary. Lightened Yuyuan Bazaar Yu Garden Lantern Festival 
2. Lujiazui & The Bund
Beyond the ever-impressive “World Architecture Expo” and the Oriental Pearl Tower, you can admire romantic violets blooming along the Bund in February. This month, visiting this area at night offers not only stunning cityscapes but also the chance to witness spectacular iron flower performances against the dazzling backdrop of the Oriental Pearl Tower.
3. Zhujiajiao Water Town
Red lanterns lined the bridges and rivers of the Water Town. Besides, folk markets and folk performances will deliver you some special festival experiences.
4. Shanghai Disney Resort
Castles and parks adorned with festival decorations, and New Year-themed parades and exclusive holiday performances can be admired.
Is February Crowded for a Visit?
That depends on the specific dates. 
Generally speaking, most of February is quiet with fewer tourists due to the somewhat cold weather of Shanghai. So, you will not feel crowded in most attractions, and spend a bit less on hotels.  Quiet Shanghai in February 
However, you should note that the period of the Chinese New Year holiday is when Shanghai is full of domestic visitors, which is usually in January or February. At that time, famous attractions like the Yu Garden, Nanjing Road, the Bund, etc., are quite crowded; long lines form for each item in Shanghai Disneyland Park; and hotels surge in their prices… In 2027, the holiday will fall from February 4 to 12. 
Tips for Visiting Shanghai in February
1. Try to avoid visiting Shanghai during the Chinese New Year holiday. On the one hand, the city will be crowded, and hotels will be quite expensive. On the other hand, some restaurants and malls will close temporarily. Don’t worry that you will miss the festival atmosphere - the decorations mentioned above will be available for more than one month.
2. Book your hotels and tickets for attractions in advance, after all, Shanghai is quite a popular tourist destination both at home and abroad.

Shanghai Weather in June
 June belongs to the summer, and Shanghai enters its plum rainy season in the middle of the month, so the weather features high temperature, high rainfall, and high humidity. If you can accept the a bit unfavorable weather of Shanghai during this month, you will be rewarded with a relatively quiet city bursting with greenery and a limited-time sea of flowers.
Rainy Season with High Rainfall and HumidityAround mid-June each year, Shanghai enters the plum rainy season, featuring frequent overcast and rainy weather. On average, this month sees the highest precipitation of the year, at 159 mm, and rainy days account for nearly half of the month. To make matters worse, the month has both persistent drizzles and sudden downpours, both of which may disrupt your outdoor plans and cause significant inconvenience.
Another characteristic of the plum rainy season is high humidity. In June, Shanghai’s average humidity is 79%, also the highest of the year, which undoubtedly makes the air feel damp and stifling. Traveling to Shanghai this month, you will find that the tissues on the table of hotels are almost always damp, and laundry takes 4-5 days or more to dry. Gloomy Shanghai in June  
High TemperatureJune marks the beginning of summer in Shanghai. While temperatures are relatively high, the frequent rainfall keeps them from becoming excessively high. On most cloudy or rainy days, high temperatures in Shanghai hover around 25-30 degrees Celsius (77-86 degrees Fahrenheit), while low temperatures are around 20°C (68°F). On most sunny days, daily highs typically range from 30 to 35°C (86-95°F), and the daily lows are around 23-25°C (73-77°F). At times, especially toward the end of the month, the daily highs can reach around 36-38°C (97-100°F).
When the temperatures rise above 35°C (95°F), there is no doubt that outdoor activities will become quite challenging. However, you should know that in June, you will not feel very cozy even on days with daily highs of around 30-35°C (86-95°F): the high humidity makes the apparent temperature much higher and creates a sticky sensation.  Hot June on Cloudy Day  
Daylight Hours & Sunshine HoursThe day turns bright quite early at 04:51-04:53 this month, and becomes dark at 18:53-19:02. As a result, Shanghai gains quite long daylight hours of over 14 hours. However, since it’s in the rainy season, the sunlight is usually blocked by clouds, and it is common to encounter overcast weather all day long. As a result, the sunshine hours are only 4-5 hours per day on average.
However, once the sun is shining, you need to take some measures to protect your skin, because the UV index can reach 11 this month.
Averages for Shanghai Weather in June
Temperature: 24°C / 75°F
High Temperature: 27°C / 81°F
Low Temperature: 20°C / 68°F
Humidity: 79%
Rainfall: 159mm
Rainy Days:15 days
Sunrise: 04:51 ~ 04:53
Sunset: 18:53 ~ 19:02
Air Quality in June
Average AQI: 37
Is June a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?It depends on the dates that you choose to travel.
Generally speaking, the scenery of Shanghai is beautiful and worth-visiting whole month. However, weather-wise, the temperature in the first half of June is slightly lower than that in the second half, and the rain usually falls not very frequently in the first half since the rainy season has not yet come. So, you can have a not-bad travel experience if you visit Shanghai during the first half of June. 
What to Pack When Visiting Shanghai in June?  Clothes: To stay comfortable in the damp and hot daytime, summer clothes as thin and breathable as possible are recommended to bring. For example, loose-fit and quick-dry tank tops, T-shirts, shorts, skirts, dresses, and thin long pants are good choices. Another piece of advice is to choose light-colored clothes that absorb less heat than dark-colored ones. Some nights may be a bit cool, so consider bringing shirts or thin jackets, which can also block the sunshine during the sunny daytime.
 Shoes: The shoes you pack should be both comfortable for walking and breathable, so try to search your shoe cabinet for cozy sandals, canvas shoes, and sneakers with breathable mesh uppers. 
 Others:
1. To prevent the harm of strong UV rays, sunglasses, sunhats, and sunscreen are needed to bring.
2. Rain is quite common in Shanghai in June, so always take an umbrella with you. Besides, you are recommended to put some travel-sized tissues in your bag for timely use.
3. With hot and humid environment, mosquitoes are rampant this month, making insect repellent sprays and stickers important.
What Does Shanghai Look Like in June?
1. June Scenery of Classic Attractions(1) The Bund: On a sunny day, the significant skyscrapers are clearly visible, with the background of blue and clear sky. On rainy days with mist, the skyline becomes hazy, and the Bund is in a quiet and unique atmosphere. From 19:00 to 23:00, a scene of dazzling lights can be seen.
(2) Zhujiajiao / Yu Garden: They are lush and green all around. In the rainy season, shrouded in misty rain, these sites take on an even more rustic and elegant charm, resembling a tranquil and poetic painting slowly unfolding before your eyes. Stunning Night View of the Bund  
2. Lively Activities(1) Activities for Dragon Boat Festival: In 2027, the Dragon Boat Festival falls on June 9. Various celebratory events will be held throughout Shanghai. For example, Zhujiajiao Water Town will feature folk performances, dragon boat races, and other Dragon Boat Festival-themed exhibitions. Of course, you can also sample zongzi, the food for the festival specially. In addition to Zhujiajiao, Yu Garden, Old City God Temple, and some malls will also host Dragon Boat Festival markets during this period.
(2) In 2027, June 16 marks the 11th anniversary of Shanghai Disney Resort. Special events will be held on that day.
Tips for Shanghai Trips in June Zhujiajiao Water Town in Rain 1. In June, Shanghai generally sees moderate visitor traffic. However, the Dragon Boat Festival holiday falling on June 19-21 in 2026 is an exception. During this short holiday, there will be a surge in domestic visitors to Shanghai, and popular attractions such as the Bund, Nanjing Road, and Shanghai Disneyland Park will experience peak crowds. So, early booking is needed if you plan to visit Shanghai during this period.
2. The sun rises early, so consider heading out early each day to explore the city, as the mornings are generally cooler. Try to avoid scheduling outdoor activities for the hottest 12:00-14:00 to prevent discomfort or even heatstroke.
3. When traveling to Shanghai in rainy June, be sure to check the weather forecast regularly. You can visit popular outdoor attractions on both sunny and drizzly days - on drizzly days, places like the Yu Garden, Zhujiajiao, and the Bund offer a different yet still beautiful scenery. If it rains heavily, visiting museums or shopping malls or similar indoor places will be a more comfortable option.

Shanghai Weather in October
 The weather of Shanghai is cool and sunny in October, perfect for various outdoor explorations. Besides, autumn colors highlight the city in the late month. 
But avoid visiting Shanghai during the National Day Holiday of China from October 1 to 7 in 2026, when hundreds of thousands of domestic tourists surge into the city.  The Bund in Sunny October  
Pleasantly Warm or Cool OverallGenerally speaking, in October, Shanghai experiences cozy and mild weather with gradually dropping temperatures day by day.
During the first half month, the daytime is kind of warm, with a temperature range of about 25-30 degrees Celsius (77-86 degrees Fahrenheit); and the nighttime is cool with the temperature hovering around 20°C (68°F). In some years, like 2025, the cold air arrives at Shanghai late, and the city may experience several hot days with the daily high of around 35°C (95°F) in early October. Take it easy, this situation is quite rare.
During the second half month, Shanghai becomes cool the whole day. Daily high is around 20-25°C (68-77°F), a level that makes you feel comfortable for outdoor activities. Daily low is stable at 15-18°C (59-64°F), pretty cool so a light jacket is necessary. Cool Late October  
Stable WeatherVisiting Shanghai in October, the chances of your trip being interrupted by rain are very slim. Though there are about 12 rainy days in Shanghai this month on average, the rain during these days is most likely to be light and short. 
Humidity is around 71% on average. Combined with the mild temperature this month, the air feels fresh and cozy, but not muggy at all. Sunny October with Blue Sky  
Daylight HoursIn October, sunsets come earlier and earlier, at around 17:40 at the beginning of the month and 17:06 by the end. With darkness falling early, the available daytime for sightseeing is reduced: this month, daylight hours are shortened from 11.5 to 10.5. So, you need to plan your itinerary carefully: on the one hand, make your daytime tours more compact; and on the other hand, plan richer activities for the nighttime. More specifically, night views of the Bund, Nanjing Road, and Yuyuan Bazaar are recommended to be added to your travel list. Besides, the Yu Garden opens at night on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays from May to October each year, providing you with a unique experience.
UV index reaches 7 the highest in September, and the sunlight is strong during the sunny moments. So, don’t forget to take some measures to protect your skin when going out.

Average AQI:38
What to Pack to Visit Shanghai in October?  Clothes for the First Half of October: You can wear short-sleeved or long-sleeved T-shirts plus thin long pants during the daytime and add a jacket for nighttime tours. 
 Clothes for the Second Half of October: Thin hoodies plus sweatpants, or short-sleeved T-shirts, thin knitwear, plus thin jeans are more comfortable for daytime, and leather jackets or denim jackets are recommended to put on during nighttime.
 Shoes: As long as they are comfortable for walking, sneakers, loafers, and canvas shoes are all OK to pack.
 Others: An umbrella is better to bring just in case. During the sunny hours, sunscreen, sunglasses, and hats are recommended to wear.
Tips for Traveling during China National Day HolidayThere is no doubt that October is one of the best months to visit Shanghai, because of the favorable climate. However, there is one thing that you should note.
National Day holiday, which is from October 1 to 7 in 2026, is one of the busiest tourist periods in Shanghai throughout the year. During this long public holiday, numerous domestic tourists stream into Shanghai. Therefore, the Bund, the Yu Garden, and the Disneyland Park will all be extremely crowded - you may even find it hard to move freely sometimes. Besides, you will inevitably spend a lot more on hotels and tickets for the Disneyland Park than usual. Crowded National Day Holiday 
Try your best not to arrange the visit to Shanghai for this period. If this is your only available time, you may want to know that:
(1) October 5-7 see fewer tourists than October 1-4.
(2) Hotel rooms and tickets for famous attractions need to be reserved ahead of time.
(3) Getting up early and finishing your trip to the most popular attractions like the Yu Garden before 10:30 can help you have a much quieter experience.
(4) For trips to Zhujiajiao Water Town, you are also recommended to arrive early to avoid main crowds.
(5) Want to see the beautiful and dreamlike night view of Lujiazui in the Bund, but wish to get rid of the crowds? The North Bund, that is, the north bank of the Huangpu River, is a good alternative. 
Travel Highlights of Shanghai in October1. During the National Day holiday, Disneyland Park will give special fireworks shows that differ from the usual ones. In the second half of October, approaching Halloween, the park will be full of Halloween-themed decorations and host various related parades in addition to the special fireworks shows.
2. By the end of October, the leaves in Shanghai begin to take on their autumn colors. At this time, there are already plenty of yellow ginkgo leaves. Guyi Garden and the “Ginkgo Alley” on Jumen Road in the city center are excellent spots for viewing them. Red maple leaves are not yet abundant, but you can look for them at places like the Yu Garden and Century Park.

 Trip Highlights
 Visit Shanghai Museum to ponder its world-class collections of ancient bronzeware, paintings, and porcelain.
 Stroll around the classic Yu Garden, renowned for its large rockeries, clear ponds, and ancient pavilions.
 Unwind at the Bund with a Huangpu River cruise, where historic Western-style architecture faces off against the soaring modern skyline.
 Browse the eateries and shops along prosperous Nanjing Road to experience the liveliest Shanghai.
 No commission-based shopping stops! More time will be spent on attractions and you’ll enjoy a pure sightseeing tour.
 No optional tours, which are just tourist traps and will always cost you more with a high markup on price.
 This trip can be customized to meet your individual needs!

Overlooking Huangpu River from Shanghai Tower0:40
Shanghai Musuem East1:00

Yu Garden ShanghaiWelcome to Shanghai! Take a bite of this alluring world-leading metropolis with its striking highlights, including classic Chinese gardens, thousand-year-old artworks, elegant Western colonial architecture, and soaring skyscrapers.
Your guide and the driver will pick you up from your hotel at approximately 9 AM and set off to Yu Garden. This 400-year-old Suzhou-style garden was originally commissioned by an ancient official as a filial tribute to his parents. Upon entering, you’ll be amazed by a 14-meter-high (46-foot) Giant Rockery, stacked up by tons of rare yellow stones and dotted with lush plants. Climb up to the top to enjoy a brilliant panoramic view. Lingering in the garden, you'll explore its well-organized layout: “dragon walls”, winding corridors over tranquil fish ponds, artificial rockeries topped with pavilions, as well as secluded paths through the groves, all contributing to a rich and varied landscape. Outside the beautiful garden lies the bustling Yuyuan Bazaar, where a grid of ancient streets is filled with handicrafts, silk products, souvenirs, and local snacks. Consider trying the handmade Nanxiang Steamed Soup Buns with super thin skin and juicy hot pork fillings, traditional pastries, or Scallion Oil Noodles at your own expense.
► FYI: If you visit during the Chinese New Year in January or February, you’ll find yourself in a dreamlike world, where the garden and the bazaar are decorated with thousands of hand-made lanterns themed around Chinese mythologies and zodiacs.
Our Guests Visiting Yu Garden, Shanghai
Our Guests in Yuyuan Bazaar
Our visit continues to the Shanghai Museum, a huge treasure trove of ancient Chinese art, especially boasting world-class exhibits of bronzeware, traditional calligraphy and paintings, as well as exquisite porcelain. The Bronze Gallery displays the most extensive bronzeware history worldwide, among which the Buffalo-shaped Ritual Wine Container, Da Ke Tripod, and Rectangular Capacity Measuring Vessel are particularly worth a careful appreciation, offering insights into the etiquette, land system, and slavery 3,000 years ago. Cherish the chance to enjoy the current calligraphy and painting artworks, which are rotated every six months, as they’re extremely sensitive to temperature, humidity, and light. During your visit, you might find that some exhibits lack specific archaeological context. There are many reasons for this: some artifacts were donated, some were repatriated from overseas, and some were even salvaged from recycling spots in the late 20th century.
Bronze Gallery in Shanghai Museum
Striking Skyline of Pudong Seen from the Bund
In the afternoon, let’s move to the city heart, the Bund, nestled along the west bank of Shanghai’s mother river, the Huangpu River. Unwind along the 1.5-kilometer-long (0.9-mi) riverside promenade, glimpse the splendid colonial-era legacy, and discover the secrets this riverbank holds. Having served as concessions from 1844 until 1943, the Bund earned the nickname "Wall Street of the East" in old Shanghai, becoming home to a lot of consulates, banks, and trading companies from various countries. Today, its 52 buildings of styles from Art Deco to modernism offer a living architectural textbook to peek at the city’s past glory. It feels as if a European metropolis has been brought to the banks of the Huangpu River. By the way, the revolving doors of the legendary Fairmont Peace Hotel on the Bund are the oldest existing automatic doors in Shanghai!
As you lean against the railing of the observation deck, you can watch the ferries on the river while gazing across at the prosperous Pudong New Area, where stand the Oriental Pearl TV Tower, Shanghai Tower, and many other high-rises, bearing witness to the city’s blossoming in the 21st century. Later, board a 1-hour Huangpu River cruise to immerse yourself in 360-degree panoramic views of this contrasting skyline from a dynamic angle.
After disembarking, follow your guide for a stroll along the famous Nanjing Road connecting with the Bund. Dubbed China’s top pedestrian street like Fifth Avenue in New York, the busy commercial avenue is home to hundreds of modern shopping malls, time-honored brands, and local specialty stores. It represents the cutting-edge technology and fashion of Shanghai, featuring flagship stores and experience centers for tech giants like Apple and Huawei.
All of our exploration concludes here. Your guide will escort you back to your hotel, or you may choose to stay longer on your own to enjoy the vibrant night views. Hope you enjoyed the day with us!
The Bund, Shanghai
Bustling Nanjing Road
► Nighttime Inspiration:
If tired of walking, try the retro tram on Nanjing Road to go back to the Bund, costing CNY 10 (USD 1.4) per person for one way. Rest your legs and enjoy the bustling street thronged with lively crowds. As the sky darkens, the city showcases its razzle-dazzle. Both banks of the Huangpu River will be illuminated by warm yellow lights and colorful neon lights, reflecting off the shimmering river surface, which creates a stunning scene that contrasts history with modernity. The lighting hours are generally between 18:00 and 22:00 or 19:00-23:00. If you happen to visit during a festival or celebration, don’t miss the gorgeous light show, lasting 5 to 10 minutes every half hour, when dazzling lights change with the rhythm of the music.

酒店位置優越，樓下有免費穿梭巴士直達迪士尼樂園，早上還可以提早一小時入園。房間充滿玩具總動員元素，小朋友特別喜歡，入住的房卡可以保留當紀念品。服務員笑臉相迎，主動提供協助，讓人感受到親切。食物選擇較少，早餐和餐飲質素一般，隔音效果不佳，房間噪音問題較大。
環境位置 (9)
酒店位置便捷，步行至迪士尼小鎮約15分鐘，酒店提供頻繁的免費接駁巴士往返樂園，距離入口非常近，特別適合帶孩子的家庭入住。酒店內部設計以玩具總動員主題為主，氛圍感拉滿，公共環境中有多處兒童游樂設施，讓小朋友在酒店內也能盡情玩樂。（根據 9 則評論）
服務質量 (5822)
酒店員工的服務態度普遍受到好評，服務親切周到，能隨時響應住客需求，提供了如行李寄存、手工活動等多樣化服務。員工會主動協助住客，並且在生日時送上祝福和小禮物，讓住客感受到賓至如歸的體驗。（根據 5,822 則評論）
設施 (12)
酒店設施新穎，客房乾淨整潔，提供兒童洗漱用品和卡通拖鞋。一樓有遊戲室可供孩子玩耍，並有手工活動及玩具總動員角色合照等體驗，增添了樂趣。房間雖不大，但維護良好，床品舒適。（根據 12 則評論）
免費接駁巴士
酒店提供免費接駁巴士服務，班次密集，方便住客往返迪士尼樂園和小鎮，節省了大量通勤時間，尤其是在節假日期間，讓出行更加輕鬆。
客人建議 (472)
少量客人建議酒店在以下幾方面改進：首先，入住流程效率低下，許多客人反映需要排隊數小時才能辦理入住，耗費大量時間。其次，對於身份驗證和入住規則的要求過於繁瑣，特別是關於家庭成員的身份確認，導致不便和不滿。最後，客人對於酒店的服務態度表示不滿，認為工作人員缺乏應有的職業素養，未能有效解決客人的問題。（根據 472 則評論）

住在這裏 感覺自己也是迪士尼的一員
住在toy story的好處是：
1. 有免費早享，提前一小時入園
2. 免費酒店接駁班車到最近的早享入口（而且是酒店專享哦，和普通早享票的入口不一樣，所以人也少）
3. 有機會和玩偶們互動！我超級幸運遇到了woody 和bo beep 非常開心
我當天是先早上早早入園，玩了4-5個熱門項目，再回去酒店吃早餐（到11am）
早餐也很豐盛💕有中餐/西餐。個人覺得pancake waffle 番茄魚都好吃耶😘
總的來説，這是個超級夢幻的體驗，我一定會再回來～

“玩具總動員飯店”的主題取材於迪士尼?皮克斯系列電影《玩具總動員》。而其設計也融入了被中國消費者廣泛認可的元素，飯店外型類似數字8及“無限”符號。數字8在中國寓意了好運，而在飯店外牆上的雲朵圖案也同樣含有“祥雲”的吉祥寓意。
“玩具總動員飯店”由胡迪牛仔翼樓和巴斯光年翼樓兩個部分組成，從空中俯瞰時，形成了一個代表無限的符號，讓人聯想到巴斯光年充滿勇氣與夢想的名言：“飛向太空，宇宙無限!”。露天的“胡迪牛仔苑”裡有一個比真人還要大的“胡迪”，騎在他的愛馬紅心身上，而“巴斯光年苑”內則有一個超大的“巴斯光年”在歡迎賓客。飯店同樣擁有豐富的設施，包括櫃檯點餐式餐廳、以玩具火箭和太空外星人為主題的戲水區、以及靈感源自《玩具總動員3》裡的抱抱熊角色的禮品店。
飯店內以《玩具總動員3》中的幼兒園命名的“陽光食滙”將是賓客用餐的好去處。在品嚐美味的同時，賓客還會驚喜地發現在頭頂上飄揚著以《玩具總動員》動畫明星為主題的中式風箏。這些風箏的靈感源於中國著名風箏之鄉——山東濰坊的傳統風箏製作工藝。

加州迪士尼介紹
加州迪士尼位於洛杉磯近郊的安納罕市（Anaheim），是全球第一座迪士尼樂園，也是華特·迪士尼唯一親自走過、見證開幕的神奇國度。
整座度假區主要由加州迪士尼樂園（Disneyland Park）與迪士尼加州冒險樂園（Disney California Adventure Park, DCA）兩大主題園區組成，兩者隔著步行廣場相對，步行僅需 1 分鐘即可切換園區。
1. 加州迪士尼樂園（Disneyland Park）：經典童話與家庭首選
加州迪士尼樂園擁有深厚的歷史情懷，全區劃分為九大主題區，整體設施溫和多元，是全年齡層與幼童家庭的必訪核心：
核心亮點：沉浸感十足的「星際大戰：銀河邊緣」、翻新重現經典的「米奇卡通城」，以及最具象徵性的睡美人城堡。
推薦必玩：星際大戰：抵抗軍的崛起、米奇和米妮的飛速鐵路、太空山。
夜間娛樂：睡美人城堡煙火秀（隨季節推出不同主題）、星戰園區光雕煙火、日間遊行。
適合族群：帶幼童同樂的家庭、星際大戰狂熱粉、熱愛經典迪士尼童話的旅人。
2. 迪士尼加州冒險樂園（DCA）：漫威、皮克斯與刺激體驗
冒險樂園的節奏明快且現代感十足，深度融合皮克斯動畫與漫威電影宇宙，擁有度假區內最刺激的高速遊樂設施：
核心亮點：全球首座「復仇者聯盟營區（Avengers Campus）」、高規格還原電影場景的「汽車總動員天地」，以及滿滿童趣的「皮克斯碼頭」。
推薦必玩：水箱溫泉鎮賽車手、銀河護衛隊：使命突圍（跳樓機）、超人特攻雲霄飛車、蜘蛛人大冒險。
夜間娛樂：皮克斯碼頭登場的「彩色世界水舞秀（World of Color）」，融合千道噴泉與經典動畫投影，視覺張力極具震撼力。
適合族群：青少年、成年旅客、皮克斯及漫威迷、追求感官刺激的玩家。

加州迪士尼門票攻略：票種挑選、最新價格表與預約三步驟
規劃加州迪士尼行程，搞懂門票規則是首要關鍵。加州迪士尼樂園度假區（Disneyland Resort）旗下擁有「加州迪士尼樂園」與「迪士尼加州冒險樂園」兩座園區，門票採取「購買門票 ＋ 入園預約（Theme Park Reservation）」雙軌制度。也就是說，買完門票後，必須至官方系統完成日期預約才能順利入園。
加州迪士尼門票怎麼選？V 妞 3 步驟快速決策
挑選門票時，依照以下三個步驟評估，就能快速找出最適合自己行程與預算的方案：
步驟一：評估天數（1 日票、2 日票、3 日票）
1 日票：時間有限、快閃洛杉磯的旅客適用，建議專注單一園區。
2 日或 3 日票：V 妞最推薦的玩法！雙園規模龐大，至少安排 2 天才能兼顧設施、夜間水舞與遊行，玩起來最從容。
步驟二：選擇「單園票（1-Park Per Day）」或「跨園票（Park Hopper）」
單園票：當日限定進出同一座樂園，價格最實惠，非常適合帶幼童或長輩的家庭，不用耗費體力在兩園之間來回奔波。
跨園票：當天 11:00 AM 之後即可自由穿梭兩座樂園。適合時間緊湊、想在同一天收集兩園夜間大秀（例如：先去冒險樂園看彩色世界水舞秀，再衝加州迪士尼看城堡煙火）的高機動性玩家。
步驟三：是否加購快速通行（Lightning Lane Multi Pass，簡稱 LLMP）
預訂門票時強烈建議直接勾選加購 LLMP。園區熱門設施動輒排隊 60–90 分鐘起跳，LLMP 能大幅縮短等待時間，還附贈全天 Disney PhotoPass 專業合照無限下載，省時又划算。
💡 V 妞門票精算心得：
最具性價比的黃金組合是「2 日單園票 ＋ 加購 LLMP 快速通關」！一天專攻加州冒險樂園、一天專攻加州迪士尼樂園，不僅省下跨園門票的差價，更能讓全家人省下排隊體力，步調最舒適。

加州迪士尼門票預約步驟教學
出發前透過中文平台預訂，省去複雜的外幣換算與繁瑣步驟，完成訂票後記得務必完成「入園日期綁定預約」：
步驟 1：查詢官網入園預約名額
出發前先前往加州迪士尼官方網站的「Theme Park Reservation Availability」行事曆，確認想去的日期兩座樂園是否都還有預約名額。
步驟 2：透過 Klook 平台快速訂票
進入訂票頁面，選擇預計入園的天數（1日 / 2日 / 3日）。
選擇票種方案：單園票或跨園票。
勾選加購 Lightning Lane Multi Pass (LLMP)。
Klook 系統會依照選取的日期自動帶入適用的 Tier 等級與當日最優惠台幣價格，不必手動研究繁瑣的票價分級，付款後即時出票。
步驟 3：收到確認憑證，至迪士尼官方 App 完成入園預約（關鍵步驟！）
收到 Klook 訂票確認信後，前往迪士尼樂園預約頁面註冊帳戶，註冊完成後，點選Link Ticket，輸入KLOOK確認信中的門票ID，綁訂好門票後，就去點選Tickets and Reservation Details，來去預約遊園日期，確保入園預約成功！
下載並打開最新版 Disneyland App，登入或免費註冊迪士尼帳號。
點擊右下角選單列，選擇 「Link Tickets and Passes」，輸入確認信中的門票 ID 號碼或掃描條碼完成綁定。
綁定完成後，點選 「Make Park Reservations」，挑選要前往的日期與首站入園園區（若購買單園票即為當日唯一的園區；跨園票則為 11:00 AM 前首先入場的園區）。
預約完成後可在 App 的「Future Plans」看到確認條碼，入園當天直接持手機 App 條碼即可感應入場！
👉 【Klook即時出票】預訂加州迪士尼門票與 LLMP 快速通關（免現場換票）
加州迪士尼快速通關攻略：LLMP、Single Pass 與 Premier Pass 比較
加州迪士尼快速通關體系全面升級，取代過去的 Genie+，分為三大層級：「Lightning Lane Multi Pass（LLMP）」、「Lightning Lane Single Pass（LLSP）」，以及最高階的 「Lightning Lane Premier Pass」。
園區占地遼闊，每日步行動輒突破兩萬步。LLMP 絕對是必買標配！將排隊動輒 60–90 分鐘的時間省下來多看一場秀或遊行，整趟旅程的體力餘裕完全不同檔次。
三大快速通關方案差異對照表
方案種類
參考價格
適用設施範圍
方案特點與權益
Multi Pass (LLMP)
約 $30–35 USD / 日
雙園大部分熱門設施（一次約一項）
必買首選，含當日 Disney PhotoPass 專業照片無限下載
Single Pass (LLSP)
約 $15–25 USD / 單項

Premier Pass (LLP)
約 $300–400 USD / 日
雙園所有閃電通道設施各玩一次
免預約時段、隨到隨玩，每日極限量的高預算頂級方案
💡 V 妞金錢與體力精算心得：
預算允許請毫不猶豫加購 LLMP！另外超級熱門的《星際大戰：抵抗軍的崛起》，單買 Single Pass 絕對值得，能優雅跳過兩小時排隊人龍。若想省 Single Pass 的錢，建議採用「開園衝刺」：開園前 45 分鐘抵達閘門，開園鐘響第一時間直奔星戰或賽車手，就能在60分鐘內搞定！
Lightning Lane Multi Pass 實戰操作四步驟
綁定門票後，全天候的核心預約流程皆在官方 Disneyland App 內完成：
綁定憑證：確認門票與 LLMP 已同步綁定於 App「Link Tickets and Passes」。
入園後預約首項設施：掃碼進園後，點開 App「Tip Board」，挑選第一項設施時段。
閃電通道掃碼驗票：於預約時間內抵達設施門口的專用通道，出示手機條碼感應入場。
解鎖下一次預約資格（二選一條件取其先）：
已體驗完畢：在設施入口感應條碼後，系統立即解鎖，可馬上預約下一項。
滿 2 小時冷卻：若預約的時段在 2 小時之後（例如 09:00 預約了 13:00 的場次），滿 2 小時（即 11:00）系統會提前解鎖下一項設施預約權限。
哪些設施適用快速通關？
加州迪士尼樂園（Disneyland Park）
🔥 只能單買 Single Pass：《星際大戰：抵抗軍的崛起》
⭐ LLMP 最優先預約推薦：米奇和米妮的飛速鐵路、太空山、蒂安娜的運河冒險
其他支援 LLMP 設施：千年隼走私者逃亡號、馬特洪峰雪橇、大雷山鐵路、幽靈公館、巴斯光年、星際遨遊
迪士尼加州冒險樂園（DCA）
🔥 只能單買 Single Pass：《水箱溫泉鎮賽車手》
⭐ LLMP 最優先預約推薦：銀河護衛隊：使命突圍（跳樓機）、超人特攻雲霄飛車、蜘蛛人大冒險
其他支援 LLMP 設施：玩具總動員瘋狂遊戲屋、遨翔天際、灰熊激流泛舟、怪獸電力公司、高飛空中學院
👉 【Klook即時出票】預訂加州迪士尼門票與 LLMP 快速通關（免現場換票）
加州迪士尼開放時間：雙園常態時段、提早入園與重要避開時段
加州迪士尼兩大主題樂園的營業時間並不相同，且會依照平假日、淡旺季及特殊節慶活動彈性調整。出發前一至兩週，務必透過官方 Disneyland App 或官網「Park Hours」行事曆查詢當日確切時刻表。
雙園常態開放時間速查表 
園區類別
常態開放時間
開園衝刺進場時間 (Rope Drop)
備註與注意事項
加州迪士尼樂園 (Disneyland Park)
08:00 – 00:00（午夜）
07:15 – 07:30 開放進入大街等候
旺季多營業至午夜 12 點，淡季平日可能於 22:00 或 23:00 閉園。
迪士尼加州冒險樂園 (DCA)
08:00 – 22:00
07:15 – 07:30 開放進入大街等候
閉園時間通常較早；秋季若遇萬聖節派對會提早清場。
V 妞時間精算：入園必備三大時程眉角
一般遊客提早 45–60 分鐘到場（開園衝刺關鍵）：
雖然官方開園時間表定為 08:00，但外圍安檢與閘門通常在 07:15 – 07:30 就會開門驗票。遊客可先走進「美國小鎮大街」拍照等候，08:00 鐘響瞬間由工作人員撤開繩索（Rope Drop）。想在開園前 30 分鐘零等待玩到王牌設施，務必在 07:15 前抵達安檢口。
官方飯店房客專屬「提前 30 分鐘入園（Early Entry）」：
入住三間官方主題飯店的房客，依然享有表定時間前 30 分鐘（07:30）入園的福利。請特別注意，目前官方實施「單日輪流指定單一園區」制度（加州迪士尼樂園為週二、四、六；加州冒險樂園為週一、三、五、日），出發前務必確認當天開放提早入場的是哪一座樂園，行程安排才不會撲空。
務必避開特殊活動「18:00 提早閉園清場」：
在秋季（8 月至 10 月）萬聖節活動期間，加州冒險樂園常舉辦獨立售票派對「Oogie Boogie Bash」，活動當日下午 18:00 就會全面清場、謝絕一般遊客。若購買「單園票」造訪冒險樂園，一定要避開派對舉辦日，否則遊玩時間會平白縮水 4 個小時！
加州迪士尼樂園Disneyland Park
加州迪士尼樂園（Disneyland Park）擁有最原汁原味的經典童話氛圍，全區共規劃為九大主題園區。整體遊樂設施風格相對溫和且注重故事沉浸感，從無身高限制的米奇卡通城，到高科技打造的星際大戰世界，適合三代同堂、親子家庭以及熱愛迪士尼經典動畫的旅人。
九大主題園區精華速覽
美國小鎮大街 (Main Street, U.S.A.)：復古 20 世紀初美國風情，通往睡美人城堡的起點，遊行與商店聚集地。
冒險世界 (Adventureland)：熱帶雨林探險，代表設施：印第安納瓊斯冒險旅程、叢林奇航。
紐澳良區 (New Orleans Square)：法國區爵士浪漫氛圍，代表設施：神鬼奇航、幽靈公館。
邊域世界 (Frontierland)：拓荒西部風情，代表設施：大雷山鐵路、馬克吐溫號蒸氣船。
河灣特區 (Bayou Country)（原動物天地）：紐奧良沼澤自然景觀，代表設施：蒂安娜的運河冒險、小熊維尼歷險記。
幻想世界 (Fantasyland)：童話城堡後方

房間整潔，布置清新浪漫，用品齊全。（基於207則評價）

title: 【上海城隍廟+豫園遊玩攻略】含到達交通、遊玩路線、美食和購物等 - Go Travelling World
text:
2026-09-11 晚風輕輕吹上海旅遊城隍廟, 豫園0 Comments 
上海城隍廟和豫園毗鄰，相距不超過百米，因此很多遊客都是把這兩個景點放在一起遊玩。
此外，城隍廟和豫園之間還有一個豫園商城，這裏不僅是一個大型購物美食商圈，而且建築大都是仿古建築，夜晚開燈會非常好看，是上海最美夜景地之一。當然不能錯過的還有外灘那邊的美景了，可以看【上海外灘一日遊】最佳遊玩路線順序推薦。
因此本篇攻略會把城隍廟、豫園、豫園商城都一起做了，希望能幫助大家更好地遊玩這裏。
延伸閱讀：【上海自由行】三天兩晚自由行全攻略，交通、行程、住宿、美食

上海豫園城隍廟遊玩常見Q&A
上海豫園城隍廟交通攻略
1、地鐵：上海市內乘坐地鐵10號線或14號線，在豫園站下車，1號出口出。(推薦搭乘地鐵，快速方便)
✅️地鐵巴士卡購買：中國大陸巴士地鐵一卡通
2、公交：
乘坐932路到城隍廟站下車;
乘坐64路、715路在複興東路光啟路站下車;
乘坐24路、581路到豫園站下車;
乘坐11路(內圈、外圈)、64路、304路夜班空調、736路、736路空調、801路、920路、926路空調、930路在新北門站下車。
乘坐11路(內圈、外圈)、64路、304路夜班空調在人民路新開河路站下車。
上海豫園城隍廟遊玩路線
上海豫園城隍廟片區遊玩路線推薦：
豫園地鐵站1號口→福佑小商品市場→童涵春堂中藥博物館→大壺春(豫園店)→豫園南門(大門)→豫園西門→九曲橋和湖心亭→挹秀樓→南翔饅頭館或綠波廊午餐→巧克力博物館→海上梨園→城隍廟→豫園商城
上海城隍廟豫園遊玩路線圖
上海豫園城隍廟遊玩景點
福佑小商品市場
豫園地鐵站1號口旁邊就是福佑小商品市場，裏面商品都可以還價，建議臉皮厚一點，不還價會虧。可以先逛逛挑選一些紀念品帶回家。
童涵春堂中藥博物館
這家百年中草藥店門口掛滿了各種香囊，不同節氣有不同的寓意!博物館位於4樓，免費開放。
大壺春(豫園店)
大壺春是上海老字號品牌，尤其以生煎包最為有名，如果是早上過來的可以來這邊吃個早餐。營業時間09:00-22:00。
豫園
豫園是一個園林景點，園內古色古香，適合拍照，每一處景致都獨特。遊玩時長大約是2小時。
上海豫園導覽圖
豫園遊玩路線推薦：
豫園南門→三穗堂→仰山堂→大假山→魚樂榭→萃秀堂→亦舫→複廊→學圃→點春堂→快樓→九獅軒→和煦堂→老君殿→會景樓→流觴亭→玉華堂→藏書樓→玉玲瓏→環龍橋→涵碧樓→內園→靜觀→洞天福地→聳翠亭→可以觀→還雲樓→古戲台→豫園西門
豫园始建于明嘉靖三十八年(1559年) ，距今已有460多年历史。主人潘允端是四川布政使，为了让辞官告老的父亲安享晚年，在祖宅西侧修建了这座园林。“豫”字取自《易经》，寓意“平安”“安泰”，也藏着“愉悦老亲”的一片孝心。
如今的豫园占地近30亩(约2万平方米) ，分为三穗堂、万花楼、点春堂、会景楼、玉华堂、内园六大景区。园内亭台楼阁、假山池水、龙墙花廊层层叠叠，被誉为 “虽由人作，宛自天开” 。#上海豫园旅游攻略
大假山(豫园精华之最)
由明代造园名家张南阳亲自设计堆叠，用2000吨武康石堆砌而成，高约14米。层峦叠嶂如真山，是江南现存明代黄石假山之最巨者——登顶可俯瞰整座园林。
玉玲珑(镇园之宝)
江南三大名石之一。相传是宋徽宗“花石纲”的遗物——就是《水浒传》里“智取生辰纲”那个“花石纲”。高约3米，石上72个孔洞，呈现“百孔淌泉，百孔冒烟”的奇观。古人说它“一炉香置孔中，则众孔皆烟”，站在石前，你会明白什么叫“皱、漏、瘦、透”。
三穗堂
堂高9米，五开间，华丽宽敞。抬头看“三穗堂”“灵台经始”“城市山林”三块贴金匾额——“城市山林”正是园主的心愿：身居闹市，却拥有山林野趣。
内园
原为城隍庙庙园，建于1709年，占地仅2亩。虽小，却有“螺蛳壳里做道场”的精妙。
豫園營業時間：9:00-16:30，16:00停止入場，周一休息。門票旺季40元，淡季30元。
豫園參觀信息：https://www.yugarden.com.cn/page/articleView/message.html
✅️門票預訂：Klook
九曲橋
豫園西門出來就可以看到九曲橋和湖心亭，不妨去走走，步步有轉，五步有彎，可以去除黴運，好運相隨。湖面上還會不定期舉辦各種主題的燈會展示。
九曲橋
挹秀樓
挹秀樓坐落在豫園商城中心，九曲橋旁邊，是一座西方歐洲風格的青磚木結構洋樓。樓內設有上下兩層回廊，建築風格別具一格，古樸典雅。
挹秀樓有著悠久的建造曆史，後經修繕成為永安抗戰文化名人館，館內展示著各類英雄事跡。
南翔饅頭店或綠波廊(午餐)
南翔饅頭店和綠波廊都是上海有名的老字號，南翔饅頭店主打小籠包和蟹黃灌湯包。
綠波廊則是國宴級別的酒樓，代表菜式有八寶鴨、糯米鴨、灌湯包、蟹粉包等。
巧克力博物館
位於舊校場路69號2-3樓。展館展示了用巧克力制成的動物展區，彌漫著濃鬱的巧克力香味，還有用巧克力制成的包包、鞋子、花瓶等。可以參觀免費，結束後還可品嘗小巧克力豆。
海上梨園
原是俯瞰豫園的一處戲台，如今已經發展成近千平方米的空中庭院。浸入式舞台呈現的傳統建築與餐飲區域完美融合，營造出優雅賞樂的奇妙氛圍。這裏會不定期舉行演出，需購票入場。
城隍廟
上海城隍廟是上海道教正一派的主要道觀之一，景點免費，不過要繳10元進香費。
城隍廟官網：https://shchm.org/shchm/
上海城隍廟導覽圖
上海城隍廟，原為金山廟(又名霍光行祠)，供奉西漢大將軍博陸侯霍光。上海城隍廟始建於明代永樂年間(1403年-1424年)，供奉敕封上海城隍神秦裕伯，是道教正一派的宮觀。
上海城隍廟供奉的城隍神為【秦裕伯】，元代進士，因道德高尚、仗義執言，被民眾尊崇。雖曾拒絕朱元璋的招攬，但後為國請命而入朝為官。羽化後，朱元璋贊其生不為臣、死當衛土，民眾遂奉其為上海城隍神，期望其守護上海安寧。
地址：上海市黃浦區方浜中路249號
交通：【地鐵10號線、14號線】豫園地鐵站7號口
門票：10元(可領三只清香)
開放時間：5月1日——9月30日，開放時間為9:00-17:00;
10月1日——來年4月30日，開放時間為8:30-16:30。(逢農曆初一、十五，本廟開放時間為清晨6:00起，如遇春節等特殊時段，開放時間以公告為准。)
城隍廟方位布局
城隍廟殿堂建築屬南方大式建築，但在建築風格上仍保持著明代格局。
整前後共三進：第一進供的是霍光;第二進供的是秦裕伯;第三進是城隍夫人。
建築沿中軸線依次排列，廟內主體建築有大殿、元辰殿、父母殿等十二個殿堂，樓下西側由南而北為三官殿、財神殿、客堂;東側由南而北為月老殿、慈航殿祈福堂。儀門對面中軸線上為霍光殿，背後連接一條通向後院的長廊，名為太歲殿。出太歲殿，即為後院，正面為城隍殿，西側為關聖殿，東側為文昌殿。
上海城隍廟各殿介紹
上海城隍廟主要殿宇有三官殿、月老殿、財神殿、慈航殿、祈福堂、霍光殿、元辰殿、關帝殿、文昌殿、城隍殿、娘娘殿、育德殿等。遊玩的時候按照建築布局從南到北遊玩即可。
山門照壁
在明朝嘉靖十四年(1535年)建造的，已有四百五十年以上的曆史。上面有四個金色大字“保障海隅”，原來是由明代上海縣知縣馮彬題寫的。
儀門
儀門是過去官衙的第二道正門，儀門前面有二副對聯。對聯的後面掛著一只很大的算盤，上刻著四個字“不由人算”。
城隍廟大殿
大殿內供奉金山神主漢代博陸侯霍光大將軍坐像，左首為文判官，右首為武判官，次為日巡與夜查，日巡、夜查以下為八皂隸。
太歲殿
又稱元辰殿、六十甲子殿。元，為“善”，元辰，就是指吉利時日的意思。因六十甲子神靈是星神，故也稱太歲神。
三官殿
三官殿中供奉的是主管【天上事務】、【地上事務】和【水中事務】的神靈，號天官、地官和水官。
月老殿
供奉月老【主姻緣】、藥王爺孫思邈【主身體健康】、車神【主路途平安】。
慈航殿
供奉眼母娘娘【主治眼疾】、慈航大士【主平安】、天後娘娘【主出海平安】。
財神殿
殿內供奉有五位財神。中間是趙公明，左面和右面是他的部下招寶天尊蕭昇和納珍天尊曹寶。在財神殿兩邊的是招財使者陳九公和利市仙官姚少司。
城隍殿
供奉的就是明代敕封的上海縣城隍【秦裕伯】，城隍殿西面為娘娘殿，供奉上海縣城隍神夫人儲氏。城隍殿東首為父母殿，殿內供奉上海縣城隍神父母。
文昌殿
文昌帝君，即梓潼帝君主管人的【功名和祿位】
關聖殿
上海城隍廟的天井左邊是關帝殿。供關聖帝君，左右供周倉、關平二位將軍，其中關帝具有【管理命祿】、【保佑科舉】等職能。
豫園商城
這裏吃喝玩樂樣樣俱全，等到晚上燈光亮起時更是美不勝收。在這裏，你可以看到古老的弄堂和高樓並存的景象，展現了上海的迷人魅力。
2027上海豫園燈會
2027上海豫園燈會
時間及活動暫未公佈
2026上海豫園燈會
2026上海豫園燈會“來大豫園過上海年”於1月26日璀璨亮燈，拉開上海年味的帷幕。豫園民俗藝術燈區將率先點亮，由此開啟一場36天的海派年味之旅。(豫園民俗藝術燈區2月16日除夕不亮燈)。
本次豫園民俗藝術燈區實行分時段憑票入場，高峰日(每周五至周日、農曆初一至初七、元宵節)14:00-22:00入場，普通日16:00-22:00入場，成人票80元，兒童票、軍人票、老年人票50元，詳見↓
今年，豫園燈會首次延伸至古城公園、方浜中路、福佑路、外灘，並通過精心設計的馬年主題燈組，巧妙地連接起BFC外灘金融中心，呈現“六區一體”的新格局。以“回家過年”為敘事主線，串聯一條由豫園到BFC再到外灘的“曆史—現代—未來”光影敘事帶，全方位打造充滿溫情、煙火氣與儀式感的“上海過年必到路線”。
在這裏，可以重溫老上海的濃鬱年味，品上海味道、逛新春市集、賞文化演繹、享科技互動、買文創年貨、購上海禮物。讓老上海人找回記憶，讓新上海人理解傳統，讓遊客體驗海派春節。市民遊客、海外賓朋都可以來到大豫園，共同體驗上海地道年味。
豫園BFC外灘以光影合體新格局，一票通玩六個燈區!
本屆燈會從單一的豫園民俗藝術燈區，擴展至覆蓋大豫園片區的六大主題燈區，形成一條從豫園延伸至BFC外灘的連貫觀燈動線。
豫園民俗藝術燈區延續文化主題
其中，市民朋友最為熟悉的豫園民俗藝術燈區推出“山海奇豫記”第四季《曠野篇》(分時段憑票入場)，將於1月26日率先點亮，以非遺燈彩技藝，融合數智光影藝術，呈現一場文化與科技的視覺盛宴。“以夢為馬，曠野生花”的主題，表達人生是“曠野”而非“軌道”，鼓勵人們在變化無常的世界中，如駿馬般踏實努力，在山海間勇敢逐夢，把內心夢想變成美好現實。
從滿載祥瑞的“福祿之門”步入璀璨燈海之中，一幅幅喜慶的楹聯承載著滿滿的年味與祝福，率先映入眼簾，與黃金廣場的巨型走馬燈相映成趣;走馬燈內玲瓏剔透的鏤空雕花與燈光交融，呈現一派“葫光流轉，萬象呈祥”的意境。漫步凝暉路，“舞馬踏福”燈組淩空飛馳，以三段不同主題詮釋三重人生意境。
轉入中心廣場，“駿馳九州，步步生花”的六匹駿馬，仿佛踏破時空，昂首飛馳在天地山海之間。一側的銀杏樹下“事事如意”燈組蘊藏著“如意繁榮”的美好寓意，為每一位遊客送上新春祝福。文昌街，融彙了從敦煌、洛陽博物館代表性館藏珍品中提取的元素，帶著吉祥如意裝點新春。
“馬躍星河，逐夢蒼穹”的場景在九曲橋緩緩展開，湖面化為星海，二十八星宿列布，現實與傳說於此交織，形成一場可步入、可觸摸的東方生活美學體驗。此外，晏海閣“馬踏飛花”、五號門“一路繁花”，與舊校場路年味市集相連，遊人可邊賞燈邊挑選新春年貨、品嘗美食風味、購買上海禮物，在光影交織中沉浸於濃鬱的節慶氛圍。
今年豫園還與小布聯名推出特別企劃。可愛的“兔小布”化身夢想播報員，悄悄藏進四個核心燈組中——黃金廣場、凝暉路、中心廣場、九曲橋。遊客在遊覽中尋找隱藏的兔小布，更有驚喜等待著大家，讓我們一起尋夢豫園，“布布”生花。
五大免費燈區特色鮮明
今年，BFC首次以風尚潮流燈區煥彩開場，全周期免費開放。BFC聯合泡泡瑪特傾情打造新春遊園會，可愛的IP們一齊換上馬年點金奔騰新裝扮，彙聚在外灘送上新春祝福，各式祈福燈組也帶來沉浸式潮玩互動體驗，更有新春點金奔騰主題快閃店呈現獨家好禮。
BFC的新春玩樂不僅於此：拍洋畫、跳房子、懷舊街機等年味體驗彙聚南區B2複古街區;外灘楓徑裝飾靈動馬燈，一系列年味市集繽紛開啟，帶來時髦年俗好禮。上海複星藝術中心以“紋”以載道——故宮博物院沉浸式數字體驗展開年，詮釋東方美學底蘊。這個春節，BFC風尚潮流燈區將打造既熟悉又充滿新意的潮流中國年，為魔都帶來五光十色的過年新樂趣。
此外，四個燈區同時免費開放，福佑路燈區以“流光巷陌，煙火福佑”營造溫暖街巷;方浜中路燈區以“萬家燈火，方浜往事”回溯上海記憶;古城公園燈區則以“闔家團圓，古城年味”洋溢團圓氣息;外灘燈區以“璀璨江岸，外灘華章”展現現代風華。四重主題交織呼應，既傳遞上海的親切年味，又閃耀時尚潮流的繽紛光彩，在點亮城市的同時，也自然而然地引領遊客步入豫園、BFC和外灘，體驗完整而層次豐富的觀燈之旅。五個免費燈區也將陸續點亮，2月1日將實現六區同亮。
上海豫園城隍廟附近美食
首先說明一下，上海豫園城隍廟片區作為旅遊熱門區域，這裏的美食小吃在整個上海來說價格也是偏貴的，所以不太建議特地來這邊吃上海美食。
不過如果來豫園和城隍廟遊玩，可以順便吃一下這邊的美食，這裏的上海特色美食還是很豐富的，老字號比較多，以下是一些推薦：
大壺春
大壺春是上海著名老字號生煎品牌，這裏的生煎以皮厚、湯汁少為特點，面皮酥脆口感紮實，配上點米醋可以解除油膩感，再搭配一碗咖喱牛肉粉絲湯就是完美的早餐搭配。
南翔饅頭店
始建於1900年，至今仍是上海品嘗小籠包的熱門去處。如果不想排隊，可以選擇外賣打包，方便外帶和品嘗。
南翔饅頭店主打鮮肉小籠包湯汁豐盈，肉質鮮嫩，42元一屜，一共6個。
豫園城隍廟美食店家分布
綠波廊
這家餐廳可是國宴級別的酒樓。特別是他們的糯米鴨，簡直是一絕，但要注意每日供應量有限。這裏的點心也好吃，有蟹黃灌湯包、蛋黃酥、玫瑰餅、青餅等。
松月樓
有百年曆史，特色淨素菜包年銷售400萬只，味道經典，馬蘭頭松子青團也很值得嘗試，美味可口。
寧波湯圓
他們的湯圓個頭大，外皮軟糯，內餡鮮美，尤其是芝麻口味。
沈大成
主打各種糕點和青團。他們家的鹹蛋黃肉松青團美味無比，肉松的鮮味和鴨蛋黃的鹹香相得益彰，是絕妙的搭配。
光明冷飲
光明是上海人民鍾愛的牛奶品牌。在將上世紀的經典光明冰磚變成飲品後，口感更加濃鬱絲滑。底部的珍珠和咖啡液則更迎合年輕人的口味。
童涵春堂
供應古方茶飲，茶品種類豐富，都是養生配方，可以在店內用餐或外帶。
城隍廟素齋
在城隍廟內(就是寺廟裏)，面條僅售20塊一碗，澆頭15塊一個，種類繁多。素菜包、蝴蝶酥、雲片糕都非常美味，值得推薦的還有大餛飩!
除了城隍廟內，城隍廟外的舊校場路開設了一條美食街，這裏有很多上海特色美食，比如臭豆腐，都能在這裏找到。
上海豫園城隍廟購物推薦
老城隍廟食品商店
上海特產推薦來這家商店，奶糖、牛軋糖、五香豆等等都可以買得到，比較推薦購買上海梨膏糖、大白兔奶糖等。
舊校場路
這條街除了有各種美食小吃之外，還有各種上海特產可以購買。
上海住宿推薦：【上海住宿酒店】上海必住的七家酒店性價比
上海豫園城隍廟遊玩常見Q&A
重要區分：豫園(明代古典園林，收費)≠豫園商城 / 老街 / 九曲橋(免費商圈);城隍廟是獨立道觀，單獨售票，很多遊客容易混淆。
Q：上海豫園值得去嗎?
值得去：想看江南古典園林、古建築、中式美學，喜歡漢服拍照、了解上海老城廂曆史，推薦進豫園園林;只打卡紅燈籠老街、九曲橋夜景、吃小吃，免費街區就足夠，氛圍感很強。
Q：豫園要買門票嗎?
豫園商城、九曲橋、豫園老街全天免費，不用門票攜程。
豫園園林(裏面的江南古園)：旺季(4.1–6.30、9.1–11.30)40 元;淡季(7.1–8.31、12.1–次年 3.31)30 元;周一常規閉園(法定節假日除外)，16:00 停止入園攜程。
城隍廟道觀：香花券 10 元，入園贈送 3 支清香，不要在外面小販手裏高價買香攜程。
優待：全日制學生、60–69 周歲老人園林門票半價;1.3 米以下兒童、70 周歲以上老人、現役軍人、殘疾人憑證免園林門票。
Q：上海豫園要逛多久?
只逛豫園園林內部：1.5 小時左右
園林 + 城隍廟道觀：2.5–3 小時
園林 + 城隍廟 + 九曲橋 + 豫園老街(含夜景)：半天(3–4 小時)
僅免費街區(九曲橋 + 老街打卡拍照吃小吃)：1–2 小時
Q：豫園裏面有什麼?
豫園園林(收費)：明代江南古典園林，核心看點：玉玲瓏(鎮園之寶，江南三大奇石)、大假山(明代黃石假山)、三穗堂、點春堂、萬花樓、龍牆、內園古戲台，亭台樓閣、池塘假山，一步一景，屬於全國文保單位攜程。
豫園商城 / 外圍免費區域：九曲橋、湖心亭茶樓、紅燈籠老街、老字號商鋪、小吃店、文創店;可以看夜景。
Q：上海城隍廟靈驗嗎?
祈福屬於傳統文化心理寄托，心誠則靈，沒有客觀層面 “靈驗與否” 的科學說法。城隍廟是上海知名的道教正一派道觀，有 600 多年曆史，上海本地人和遊客常來祈福，求平安、事業、姻緣等，更多是一種心願寄托。
Q：上海城隍廟拜什麼?
主殿供奉上海城隍秦裕伯(城市保護神)，大殿先拜城隍;各殿分管不同祈願：
財神殿：五路財神，求財運、事業順遂
月老殿：求姻緣、良緣
三官殿：三官大帝，消災解難、祈求順遂
太歲殿：拜太歲，適合本命年
慈航殿：慈航、媽祖、眼光娘娘，可求平安、護佑家人等
 城隍廟, 豫園 
 Written by 晚風輕輕吹

11天中国经典之旅：北京、西安、桂林和上海 
这条精心设计的11天中国经典之旅，将带您全面舒适地领略中国风情。从漫步北京长城、探寻故宫的神秘，到乘船游览漓江，欣赏壮丽的石灰岩山峰，再到感受现代上海的活力，这段旅程将历史、文化、自然和都市生活完美融合，为您打造一段难忘的中国之旅。 
 定制此行程
 11 Days / 10 Nights 
 中国经典影片精华片段，节奏把握得当。 
 北京 → 西安 → 桂林 → 上海 
 最受欢迎的中国经典路线。 
 私人旅游体验 
 私人导游、司机，行程安排灵活。 
 非常适合初次到访者 
 中国入门指南。 
主页 / 十大旅游线路 / 11天中国经典之旅：北京、西安、桂林和上海
这段旅程有何不同之处 
 一家在香港注册的旅行社 
 由香港集团支持，在中国各地设有本地团队。 
 安全付款 
 可使用 Visa、MasterCard、Apple Pay、PayPal 或银行转账安全支付。 
 24/7客服支持 
 在您前往中国之前、期间和之后，我们将为您提供真正的人工帮助。 
 定制体验 
 根据您的兴趣和旅行方式量身定制活动和行程节奏。 
推荐的11天中国经典行程 
 天目的地体验焦点
 第 1-4 天中国长城漫步、故宫、天坛、静谧颐和园
 第 5-6 天西安兵马俑、古城墙、穆斯林街区及当地文化
 第 7-9 天桂林、阳朔漓江游船之旅，欣赏石灰岩山峰和乡村风光
 第 10-11 天上海外滩、上海中心大厦天际线、新旧城市对比
这段旅程是如何无缝衔接的 
这条精心设计的路线连接了中国西南地区最具标志性的自然景点，将成都、九寨沟、黄龙和张家界连接起来，使旅程流畅而节奏适宜。
为了确保旅途舒适高效，我们采用高速列车短途出行，国内航班长途出行，并根据需要提供私人接送服务。这种平衡的出行方式最大限度地减少了旅途时间，同时最大限度地增加了您亲近自然的时间，让您能够以轻松的节奏旅行，悠闲地享受每个目的地。 
国内长途航班
高速列车用于短途线路 
这条为期11天的中国经典之旅有何不同之处 
这条为期11天的中国经典之旅专为那些想要体验更深度文化之旅的旅行者而设计。每一项体验都经过精心挑选，旨在提供更深入的文化洞察、更顺畅的旅程以及更真实的中国体验。 
揭开中国皇宫不为人知的故事
探索紫禁城较为安静的殿堂，通过讲故事的方式了解皇帝、妃嫔和朝廷官员的真实生活，这是普通观光旅游中很少见到的。 
领略长城的不同风貌 
漫步慕田峪长城风景优美的一段，感受其恢弘的气势和精湛的工程技艺。部分行程还包含欣赏司马台长城迷人的夜景。 
品尝正宗北京美食 
在当地知名餐厅品尝正宗北京烤鸭，体验超越旅游菜单的城市饮食文化。 
超越第一印象 
参观兵马俑，在专业导游的带领下，深入了解秦始皇的军队、工艺和古代军事体系。 
乘船游览中国最具标志性的风景 
在漓江上乘坐游船放松身心，欣赏壮丽的石灰岩山峰、河畔村庄以及20元人民币纸币上描绘的风景。 
从外滩的历史故事到天际线景观 
漫步于历史悠久的外滩，聆听上海黄金时代的故事，然后登上上海中心大厦，俯瞰现代中国的全景。 
真实旅行者时刻 
快速了解一下这次私人旅行的体验——从北京到上海，真实的旅行者照片、当地风情和正宗的中国美食。 
详细的11天中国经典行程安排 
以下是建议的每日行程安排。所有细节均可根据您的兴趣、旅行节奏和时间安排进行调整。 
 第一天——抵达北京 | 中国之旅顺利开启 
欢迎来到中国首都北京。
抵达北京首都国际机场后，您的私人导游将在到达大厅迎接您，并乘坐舒适的私人车辆护送您前往酒店。
您的导游将协助您搬运行李和办理酒店入住，确保您轻松抵达。当天剩余时间您可以自由休息或在附近散步，以便从旅途疲劳中恢复过来，并调整到当地时间。
为什么选择这一天很合适：
✔ 没有观光压力
✔ 是时候休息和适应了
✔ 自抵达之日起提供个人协助 
 第二天——北京精华游 | 天坛与故宫 
早餐午餐
清晨，您可以从天坛开始您的一天，这里曾是历代皇帝祈求五谷丰登的地方。您还会看到当地居民练习太极拳、跳舞和其他传统运动，让您一窥北京的日常生活。
在一家颇受欢迎的当地餐厅享用正宗中式午餐后，步行穿过天安门广场，进入故宫——世界上规模最大、保存最完好的皇家宫殿。您的导游不会带您走人潮拥挤的路线，而是会带领您游览较为安静的区域，并为您讲述皇室生活、宫廷礼仪以及明清两代的历史故事。
可选定制：
胡同人力车之旅
当地市场考察
在当地家庭制作饺子
导游会根据您的兴趣调整行程节奏和重点。 
 第三天——长城体验 | 风景漫步与标志性景观 
早餐后，驱车前往慕田峪长城，这里以秀丽的景色和保存完好的古道而闻名。在导游的带领下，您可以悠闲地漫步长城，细细品味其雄伟的规模、精湛的工程技艺以及周围壮丽的山景。
对于想要体验特别之旅的旅客，部分行程可能包括下午参观司马台长城，您可以欣赏到夜晚灯光璀璨的长城——与白天的参观视角截然不同。
这一天为何如此特别：
✔ 均衡的步行时间
✔ 风景优美、人流较少的路段
✔ 可选择体验夜间活动，无需承担任何义务
餐食： 早餐+午餐
个性化提示：
想轻松游览？那就选择慕田峪，乘坐往返缆车吧。
想要更惊艳的体验？那就添加司马台夜景（季节性）吧！ 
 第四天——颐和园和西安高铁 
早餐午餐
早餐后，返回北京参观颐和园，这座中国园林艺术的杰作，是昔日皇室休闲生活的完美典范。漫步于静谧的湖泊、典雅的走廊和幽静的花园，感受昔日帝王和皇室成员的休憩之所。
下午，前往火车站，搭乘高铁前往西安。这段高效的铁路旅程让您能够舒适地穿梭于中国各大城市之间，同时体验中国现代化的基础设施。
抵达后，当地导游将迎接您并护送您前往位于市中心的酒店。
为什么选择这一天很合适：
✔ 均衡游览，不赶时间
✔ 北京和西安之间的平稳过渡
✔ 乘坐高速列车享受舒适的旅程 
 第五天——兵马俑和古城墙 
早餐午餐
今天，你将探索世界上最重要的考古发现之一——兵马俑。
参观博物馆群，欣赏为守护秦始皇陵而建造的庞大地下军队。导游将为您讲解这些兵马俑的制作、排列和保存方式，帮助您了解它们在中国古代历史上的重要意义。
下午，参观西安古城墙，它是中国保存最完好的城墙之一。您可以沿着城墙漫步或​​骑行，欣赏西安内城的全景，感受古代遗迹与现代生活交相辉映的景象。
体验亮点：
✔ 兵马俑及专家讲解
✔ 古城墙漫步或​​骑行
✔ 深入了解中国帝国军事史 
 第六天——西安市区观光及飞往桂林 
早餐午餐
今天的行程从陕西历史博物馆开始，馆内展出数千件文物，展现了中国文明历代发展历程。之后前往大雁塔，这座地标性建筑与佛教在中国的传播密切相关。
随后，您将游览热闹的回民街，这里以熙熙攘攘的氛围、传统小吃和充满活力的当地文化而闻名。导游将为您介绍当地特色美食，并讲解不同社群如何塑造了西安的历史。
下午，前往机场搭乘国内航班前往桂林，欣赏中国著名的山水风光。
为什么旅行者喜欢这一天：
✔ 对西安历史重要性的清晰概述
✔ 地道的当地市场氛围
✔ 与中国南方交通便捷 
 第七天——龙脊梯田与少数民族文化 
早餐午餐
早餐后，驱车前往龙脊梯田，这里是中国最令人叹为观止的农业景观之一。龙脊梯田依山而建，历经数百年，随着季节变换色彩——春天水波荡漾，秋收时节金黄灿烂。
漫步于层层叠叠的梯田之间，从观景台俯瞰山谷全景。了解当地壮族和瑶族少数民族如何适应山区生活，并保留了传统的木屋、耕作方式和习俗。
与当地家庭共进午餐，体验当地文化，例如制作竹筒饭和品尝新鲜制作的油茶。此次行程让您有机会深入了解远离中国大城市的乡村生活。
这一天为何如此特别：
✔ 壮观的梯田景色
✔ 体验地道的少数族裔文化
✔ 步行速度适中，沿途风景优美 
 第 8 天 — 漓江游船 |桂林飞往阳朔 
早餐午餐
今天我们将体验中国旅游中最具标志性的体验之一——漓江游船之旅。
悠闲地乘船游览，欣赏江水蜿蜒流经壮丽的石灰岩山峰、竹林和宁静的村庄。沿途，您或许会看到农民在稻田里劳作，水牛在河中嬉戏，构成一幅幅如诗如画的画面，展现了桂林的自然之美。
午后早些时候在阳朔下船，您可以游览以热闹氛围和特色小店而闻名的西街。之后前往位于郊区的酒店，享受悠闲时光。
阳朔可选活动：
烹饪课
太极拳课程
骑自行车穿过乡村 
 第9天——乡村生活及飞往上海 
早餐午餐
上午可以探索阳朔乡村，穿梭于宁静的村庄和乡间小路。这里与中国的大城市形成鲜明对比，展现了日常生活的另一面。
参观当地集市，了解村民如何购买日常必需品。导游会讲解当地的食材和习俗，帮助您更好地了解乡村传统和价值观。
下午，前往机场搭乘国内航班飞往中国最具活力的现代化城市上海。
为什么旅行者喜欢这一天：
✔ 地道的乡村生活体验
✔ 深入了解当地农民的日常生活
✔ 从自然到现代中国的平稳过渡 
 第十天——上海精华游 | 古老与现代的中国 
早餐午餐
抵达上海，中国最具国际化和活力的现代化都市。今天，您将探索上海古今交融的迷人景象，殖民历史、传统文化与未来主义的摩天大楼在此和谐共存。
从上海标志性的外滩开始您的旅程。漫步于始建于20世纪初的历史建筑之间，了解上海如何发展成为全球贸易中心。您的导游将分享一些鲜为人知的故事，揭示这座城市不为人知的过去。
继续前往法租界，这里以绿树成荫的街道、欧式建筑和轻松的氛围而闻名。这片区域让您得以一窥上海的历史街区和日常生活。
午餐后，登上中国最高的建筑——上海中心大厦。从观景台上，您可以饱览城市天际线的全景——与下方历史悠久的外滩形成鲜明的视觉对比。
晚上，您可以选择乘坐黄浦江游船，或者放松身心，悠闲地欣赏上海迷人的夜景。
这一天为何给人留下深刻印象：
✔ 新旧中国对比鲜明
✔ 步行和观光节奏均衡
✔ 从上海中心大厦欣赏标志性的天际线景观

title: 上海大自然野生昆虫馆 - 活体昆虫生态展示馆 - LoongWander
text:
上海大自然野生昆虫馆，又名东方明珠·爬宠昆虫探索中心，位于上海市浦东新区世纪大道1号东方明珠电视塔一层商业中心内（原地址为浦东新区丰和路1号），地处陆家嘴核心商圈，紧邻东方明珠塔与国际会议中心。该馆是由中新合资打造的国内首家以活体昆虫与两栖爬行动物为主的科普展示馆，荣获全国科普教育基地与上海市科普基地称号。场馆总面积为3000至3500平方米，分为上下两层，整体建筑通过高科技造景，高度模拟还原了水域、沙漠、雨林、岛屿、沼泽等多种自然生态环境。馆内共展示了300余种、数万件活体动物与标本展品，涵盖各类昆虫、两栖动物、爬行动物及小型哺乳动物，是集旅游观光、科普教育、亲子互动于一体的特色主题展馆。
历史文化
上海大自然野生昆虫馆正式建立于2001年9月23日，自诞生起便填补了国内活体昆虫与爬虫类科普展馆领域的空白。建馆之初，场馆便引进了国外先进的活体昆虫养殖技术，致力于真实展现昆虫与两爬动物的本能与习性，将因城市开发而逐渐消失的生物重新呈现于公众面前，引导大众以尊重与热爱的态度看待生命。
场馆最初位于浦东新区丰和路1号，内部划分为生态园、昆虫长廊、生态触摸区、两栖爬虫溶洞区、热带雨林区、科普教室等13个特色区域。2012年，馆内新增淡水观赏虾展区，并对昆虫长廊进行了升级改建，进一步提升了亲子互动体验。2025年9月，昆虫馆整体搬迁至东方明珠电视塔一层，并更名为“东方明珠·爬宠昆虫探索中心”，在保留原有珍贵馆藏的基础上，优化了动物生态环境，增加了更多零距离互动与科普环节，开启了全新的互动式自然科普模式。历经二十余年发展，这里已成为上海重要的自然科普地标与亲子研学目的地。
主要景点
蝴蝶生态园
蝴蝶生态园是馆内最具观赏性的区域之一，园内模拟热带蝴蝶栖息地，种植大量蜜源植物与花卉。这里生活着数十种色彩斑斓的蝴蝶，包括蓝摩尔蝶等珍稀品种，游客可观赏到蝴蝶在花丛中翩翩起舞的景象。每日14:00会定时举行蝴蝶放飞仪式，翅膀上的磷粉在阳光下折射出彩虹般的光芒。
蝴蝶生态园
昆虫长廊
昆虫长廊是活体昆虫的主要展示区，汇聚了来自世界各地的数百种奇特昆虫。游客可在此近距离观察竹节虫、独角仙、锹形虫、螳螂、蜘蛛、蝎子等生物。展区通过微缩景观还原其原生环境，展示昆虫的伪装、捕食、栖息等行为，部分透明饲养箱可让游客清晰观察昆虫的细微结构与生活习性。
昆虫长廊
两栖爬虫溶洞区
该区域以溶洞景观为背景，主要展示蜥蜴、蛙类、蝾螈等两栖与爬行动物。内部环境湿润幽暗，模拟了热带雨林与地下洞穴的生态，游客能看到绿鬣蜥、变色龙、箭毒蛙等珍稀物种。区域内造景逼真，岩石、流水、绿植交织，仿佛置身于野外秘境。
两栖爬虫溶洞区
龟鳖展示区（灵龟百态）
龟鳖展示区汇聚了全球多种龟类与鳖类，包括陆龟、水龟、半水龟等不同生态类型。既有体型庞大的亚达伯拉象龟，也有小巧玲珑的巴西龟、鳄龟等。展区分为水陆两域，游客可观赏到龟群在水中畅游、岸边晒背的悠闲场景。
龟鳖展示区
蛇蟒区
蛇蟒区安全展示了多种无毒蛇与蟒蛇，如玉米蛇、王蛇、球蟒等。每个饲养箱都配备了温控与景观系统，模拟温带、热带森林环境。饲养箱采用防爆玻璃设计，游客可安全观赏蛇类的爬行、蜕皮与进食状态。
蛇蟒区
生态触摸区
生态触摸区是亲子互动的核心区域，饲养着性格温顺、适合接触的小动物。在工作人员指导下，游客可亲手触摸羊驼、垂耳兔、龙猫等温顺动物，部分时段还可体验触摸蜥蜴、无毒蛇蜕下的皮肤，感受不同生物的独特质感。
生态触摸区
水域触摸区
水域触摸区设有浅水池与透明水族箱，展示锦鲤、淡水虾、小型两栖类等水生生物。游客可在此体验捞小鱼、投喂锦鲤等活动。此外，该区域还展示了二十多种来自国内不同流域的环境指示鱼类，用以科普河道生态健康知识。
水域触摸区
标本创意室与科普教室
标本创意室陈列着数万件珍贵昆虫标本，包括蝴蝶、甲虫、蛾类等，其中不乏珍稀濒危品种。科普教室则定期开展科普讲座与DIY活动，游客可在此学习昆虫知识，并亲手制作蝴蝶、甲虫标本作为纪念。
标本创意室与科普教室
游玩路线
上海大自然野生昆虫馆采用单层连贯式游览路线，全程约2至3小时。游客从入口进入后，首先抵达蝴蝶生态园，观赏蝴蝶飞舞与放飞仪式；随后沿通道进入昆虫长廊，逐一观赏各类活体昆虫；接着前行至两栖爬虫溶洞区，探索蜥蜴与蛙类世界；之后依次游览龟鳖展示区、蛇蟒区，了解爬行类动物；随后到达水域触摸区，体验水生生物互动；再进入热带雨林区，感受沉浸式雨林氛围；穿过雨林后，抵达生态触摸区与萌宠乐园，参与动物互动与观看表演；最后参观标本创意室与科普教室，结束全程游览。
游玩建议
建议游玩时长为2至3小时，预留充足时间参与互动与科普活动。
优先选择工作日早晨入馆，游客较少，体验更佳。
春秋季为最佳游览季节，夏季馆内温度较高（部分区域28℃以上），建议穿着轻便透气衣物。
周末及节假日11:00、14:30有小动物剧场表演，可提前规划时间观看。
参与触摸互动前，务必听从工作人员指导，仅触摸指定温顺动物。
在科普教室可参与标本制作DIY，适合亲子共同体验。
馆内设有休息区与商店，可中途休息并购买昆虫主题文创产品。
建议与东方明珠、上海海洋水族馆等周边景点串联游览。
注意事项
馆内严禁使用闪光灯拍照，强光会伤害昆虫与爬虫类生物的视觉系统。
禁止拍打、敲击玻璃饲养箱，避免惊扰动物。
未经工作人员允许，严禁擅自触摸、投喂非互动区动物。
儿童必须由成人全程陪同，不可脱离监护单独行动。
部分展区（如热带雨林）湿度高、气味较重，敏感人群可自备口罩。
馆内禁止携带宠物、食品及有色饮料入内。
触摸动物后，需在指定区域洗手，保持卫生。
遵守闭馆时间，闭馆前30分钟停止入馆。
交通
地铁：乘坐地铁2号线、14号线至陆家嘴站，2号口出站，步行约5至10分钟即达东方明珠塔一层。
公交：乘坐81路、82路、85路、798路、870路、985路、774路、939路至陆家嘴环路丰和路站，步行约5分钟。
观光隧道：从浦西外滩经外滩观光隧道至浦东，出口后往北步行约300米即达。
自驾：导航至东方明珠停车场，位于丰和路与滨江大道交叉口。
开放时间
周一至周四的开放时间为9:00至17:00，16:30停止入馆；周五至周日及国家法定节假日开放时间为9:00至17:30，17:00停止入馆。
门票
门票88元/人。可在微信中搜索服务号“上海大自然野生昆虫馆”，获取最新动态或在线购票。

title: Shanghai Wild Animal Park, Shanghai Zoological Park
text:
Home
 Destinations
 Shanghai 
 Shanghai Wild Animal Park 
There are many rare and endangered animals at the Shanghai Wild Animal Park, at Sanzao Town in Nanhui District, about 35 kilometers from the city center. The park is one of China's biggest wild animal parks and covers an area of 153 hectares. There are over 200 rare species and over 10,000 animals from all over the world, including giraffe, zebra, white rhinoceros and hunting leopards. Some indigenous animals under special protection include giant pandas, golden monkeys, south-china tigers, and Asian elephants and many others.
The Shanghai Wild Animal Park is divided into two areas: one for walking, and one which is accessible to buses. There is a herbivore zone, a free zone, aquatic bird lake, bird zone, animal kindergarten, pet monkey park, rare animal park, animal performance zone, sea lion performance zone and other spots in this Park.
The walking area allows a close look at many gentle animals on foot. During a leisurely walk you will see Australian kangaroos, Asian Sika deer, African ring-tailed lemurs and Latin American yellow and blue macaws and more.
The bus enclosure takes you among zebra, yak, deer, elephant and some other fierce beasts. Be forewarned though: the bus park is not suitable for all, especially young children or those with a delicate temperament. Sometimes, you may encounter unpleasant even gruesome sight.
There is also a special animal zoo which is a hit with small kids where they can have a close-up look at the lovely animals.
Travel Essentials
Tickets: 130 RMB (about 18 USD) for adults; children between 6 and 18, 65 RMB (about 9 USD); for children under 1.3 meters (4.3 feet) or under 6 years of age, admission is free.
Location: 178 Nanliu Main Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai
Chinese: 上海野生动物园 Shànghǎi Yěshēng Dòngwù Yuán
Times: July and August, 8:00 am to 6:00 pm; March to June and September to November, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm, and December to February, 8:30 to 4:30.

text:

 Trip Highlights
 Appreciate the old stone-gate buildings in Xintiandi, a brilliant fusion of Chinese and Western architecture.
 Stroll along the soul-stirring alleys shaded by Platane trees and lined with boutiques, cafes, and knickknack shops.
 Visit the elegant former residences of Chinese celebrities in the 1920s, such as Soong Ching-ling or Zhou Enlai.
 Sip a cup of tea or coffee and observe the vibrant and diverse scene of local young people.
 This trip can be customized to meet your individual needs!
Welcome to find Shanghai's hidden gems in its tree-lined historical streets. Take in the old charming vibe from the age-old stone-gate architecture to exquisite boutiques, cozy cafes and tea houses, European-style mansions, and Art Deco buildings. 
► Duration: 4 to 5 hours
► Start Time: Flexible. 9:00 or 14:00 are most recommended. Discuss custom times with your travel consultant in advance.
► Walking Distance: 5-6 km (3.1-3.7 mi)
At the agreed time, your guide will pick you up from your hotel and then take a taxi or metro to Xintiandi Neighborhood. Here, you’ll admire the stone-gate (Shikumen) buildings, which retain classic elements outside, such as mottled exposed brick walls, symmetrical lintel carvings, and black lacquered doors with copper rings, while their old interiors have been transformed into trendy shops, art spaces, and specialty restaurants, achieving a coexistence of the old and the new and a fusion of Chinese and Western styles. Walk along the smooth, weathered stone paths, and appreciate alleyways that carry the everyday charm of old Shanghai. The red walls and gray tiles of the stone gate houses, bathed in light and shadow, bear the wrinkles of bygone days; just a few steps away, the lights in the floor-to-ceiling shop windows shimmer with modern brilliance. We’ll also drop by the unassuming architecture, the Site of the First National Congress of the Communist Party of China, a meaningful landmark, engraved with the deep history of the country’s past.
Retro Red-brick Houses in Former French Concession
Retro-style Mansions, Shanghai
We'll then stroll to the 120-year-old Fuxing Park, a calming green space designed in a French-style in 1900. Here stands a century-old sycamore tree, known as the "second oldest in Shanghai," and to the north stands a double statue of Marx and Engels. Enjoy a leisurely stroll and take in the serene ambience.
After that, start your Sinan Road exploration. The pedestrian-only street is designated as a historical preservation road that will never be widened or used by public transportation, and is hailed as a "living history book of the city." Strolling along it, you can directly experience the architectural panorama of Shanghai-style buildings and garden villas from the 1920s and 1930s. There are 51 garden villas of different styles, including Spanish, English, French, Art Deco and Sino-Western fusion architectural styles, lining the 1.4-km-long (0.87-mi) Sinan Road, shaded by dense Platane trees. The elegant cluster of buildings is called Sinan Mansions, and each carries its own unique story, with some concerning the rise and fall of a notable family, and others the changing eras. You can drop by anyone you like, such as the former residences of China’s first Premier Zhou Enlai (1898-1976 AD) and the legendary Peking Opera master Mei Lanfang (1894-1961 AD). The retro-style three-story Sinan Bookstore, transformed from warlord Feng Yuxiang’s (1882-1948 AD) former residence, is also worth lingering over, and it collaborates with the 15-year-old London Review Bookshop, offering a dedicated section for new English books.
Afterward, walk north to Nanchang Road, a large residential area with many old alleys tucked away. Every corner holds unexpected surprises as the entire street is filled with an artistic and pleasant atmosphere, thanks to a pretty mix of creative boutiques, including niche crystal shops, clothing stores, leather goods stores, and vintage jewelry shops. Feel free to browse at your own pace.
Next, we’ll head to the beating heart of the district, Middle Huaihai Road, a vibrant, trendy commercial hub, home to many trendy brands and artistically designed storefronts. Capture a stunning picture with the giant robot face at the Gentle Monster to hoover up Instagram likes, explore the world's first FARM BOB flagship store, famous for its scarecrow rock figurine wall packed with brightly colored toys and vinyl figures, and experience Japanese lifestyle design at MUJI, which sells high-quality cups, stickers, kitchenware, and more. The used bookstore hidden on the street corner houses a collection of Hong Kong and Taiwan editions and other rare books. The quiet and pleasant atmosphere makes it a perfect place to stop and read, enjoying a moment of peace.
Former Residences of Celebrities in the 1920s
Wukang Mansion, Shanghai
 ★ Special Treat: Coffee Break at Anfu RoadContinue west to Anfu Road, which offers a vivid snapshot of local young people chatting over coffee outdoors, or you can see fashion lovers get in and around the trendy shops. The area is paired with a growing number of cafes and tea houses, and we’ll include one especially for you! Linger over a morning coffee or an afternoon tea, and savor the century-old taste along with the modern fashion of Shanghai. 
Walk till the end of Anfu Road, and turn onto Wukang Road. Time and space shift instantly. This is not only the heart of Shanghai's trendsetters but also a serene outdoor museum of European architecture. Your guide will point out “Romeo’s Balcony” to you, which refers to the semicircular cantilevered balcony on the second floor of a Spanish-style villa with a red-tiled roof and exquisite cast-iron decorative railing. Locals romantically called it Romeo's Balcony, and the name borrows from the classic balcony scene in Shakespeare's play “Romeo and Juliet”. Stop by the cozy Ferguson Lane, home to award-winning restaurants, galleries, designer boutiques, florists, beauty salons, wineries, and vegetarian restaurants. Also, drop by the Old House Art Center, which showcases the history of the century-old buildings and you can observe the pictures, mini models, and paintings to get a deep insight into the details. From the outside, admire the Former Residence of Soong Ching-ling (1893-1981 AD), honorary president of the People's Republic of China and the wife of Dr. Sun Yat-sen (1866-1925 AD), the founder of modern China. Glimpse this elegant Western-style courtyard, featuring a unique red-tiled, ship-shaped main building nestled in a garden of century-old camphor trees.
Today’s final stop is the landmark building, Wukang Mansion, located at the intersection of five streets. Designed by a Hungarian architect in the 1920s, the giant ship-shaped building in French Renaissance style is unique for its triangular shape, due to the triangular terrain. Look at its facade clad in yellowish-brown bricks and continuous arched corridors, and don’t miss capturing a memorable photo with it. Shanghai City Layout
As one of the mega-cities in China, Shanghai occupies an area of over 6,300 square kilometers (2,400 square miles) with a population of over 24 million. Shanghai city layout can be divided into two main parts which called Pudong and Puxi by Huangpu River. Shanghai central urban area eventually spread from People’s Square & the Bund.
Shanghai Urban AreaThe city now includes 16 districts, which can be divided into 4 parts:
 7 Central Areas: Huangpu, Jing’an, Xuhui, Changning, Yangpu, Hongkou, Putuo
 1 Semi urban & Semi suburb: Pudong New Area
 3 Suburban Areas: Minghang, Baoshan, Jiading
 5 Remote Suburbs: Songjiang, Jinshan, Qingpu, Fengxian, Chongming
Downtown Landmarks and Area Guide
The BundThe Bund in Huangpu District, also called East Zhongshan 1st Road, is located in the west bank of Huangpu River. As an important symbol of the city, it owns 52 buildings in different architectural styles. When night comes and neon lights on, the Bund provides the most beautiful scene of Huangpu River, Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower and World Financial Center. Taking a Huangpu River cruise is the best way to enjoy the modern style of new Shanghai. Besides, the Sightseeing Tunnel connecting the Bund and Oriental Pearl Tower is worth a try!
People's Square – City CenterAs one of the landmarks, People’s Square in Huangpu District covers an area of 140,000 square meters (170,000 square yards). Known as ‘Urban Green Lung’, it’s surrounded by many famous attractions nearby: Madame Tussauds Shanghai in the north, Urban Planning Exhibition Hall in the northeast, Shanghai Grand Theatre in the northeast, and Shanghai Museum in the south. The popular Hong Kong Shopping Center is in the underground passage of the square. Visitors can find all kinds of stuffs there like clothes, jewelry, gifts and snacks. People’s Square can be easily accessed by public transportation Metro Line 1, Metro Line 2 and Metro Line 8. Nanjing Road   The Bund  
Nanjing Road & Huaihai RoadThese two in Huangpu District are the two most famous shopping streets according to Shanghai city layout. The known Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street provides many things like clothes, gifts, local snacks, and Chinese handcrafts. As for Huaihai Road, it normally refers to 2,200-meter-long Middle Huaihai Road Commercial Street, which is the section from South Shaanxi Road to South Nanjing Road. Along the street, there are some branded shopping centers like K11, IAPM Mall and Parkson.
Pudong Lujiazui Financial AreaLujiazui in Pudong New Area, facing the Bund in the other side of Huangpu River, is one of the most renowned financial centers in China, covering many headquarters of multi-national banks. The highest building in China, Shanghai Tower, with the height of 632m (2,073 feet) is also located here. Besides, the 492-meter-high (1,614 feet) Shanghai World Financial Center in Lujiazui is the highest flat-roof building in the world. As an important business area, it also owns grand shopping centers like Super Brand Mall and IFC Mall; for sightseeing, Oriental Pearl Tower, Jin Mao Tower and Ocean Aquarium are suggested.
Shanghai Old Street & Old City God Temple Yuyuan Garden Area, Shanghai As one of downtown landmarks in Shanghai layout, the Old Street in Huangpu District preserves the old banks, jewelry stores, tea houses and drama stages in the city. The street is divided into two sections by Guanyi Street: the east section keeps residential characteristics of the late Qing Dynasty and the early Republic of China; while the west section imitates local residences in Ming and Qing dynasties. Many time-honored shops are still open in this area like Tonghanchun Medicine Store, Old Shanghai Tea House, Chunfeng Deyi Tea House, Wuliangcai Glasses and Deshun Restaurant.
The Old City God Temple is near the Old Street, and this area has developed as a popular shopping place for souvenirs and small wares. The shopping area near the temple and Yuyuan Garden mainly provides local snacks like Nanxiang Steamed Stuffed Bun, stinky tofu, and Crab-Yellow Pastry. Every Lantern Festival, there is a temple fair near the temple. Visitors can not only buy some snacks and handcrafts but also enjoy many folk performances.
Shanghai French ConcessionFormer French Concession, stretching across Huangpu District and Xuhui District, is full of western style houses. When autumn comes, the phoenix tree leaves become the best decoration of these architectures. Many historical and cultural relics are standing in this area, like Former Residence of Sun Yat-sen, Sinan Mansions, and Former Residence of Chow En-Lais. Besides, an art area, Tianzifang is also located in the French concession. Young people can enjoy themselves in the bars, cafes, crafts shops and boutiques providing here.
XujiahuiShanghai city layout indicates that Xujiahui Shopping Area in Xuhui District extends to Wanping Road in the east, Yishan Road in the west, and stretches to Guangyuan Road in the north and Linglin Road in the south. It owns many grand shopping malls like Grand Gateway 66, Orient Shopping Center, Pacific Department Store, Huijin Department Store, and Metro City, providing luxuries, middle-high class clothes and foods. Among all kinds of commodities, digital products selling in this area are the most popular ones among customers.
Suburban Layout Guide for TouristsShanghai city layout of the suburb tells about the Disneyland Park in Pudong New Area, which is the first one in China. In this theme park, tourists can enjoy the largest Disney castle, the largest Disney parade and the first Pirate-themed Park in the world. Form People’s Square, visitors can take the metro to the park within 1 hour.
Identify and Locate a Road in ShanghaiNearly all the roads in the city was named regularly. The north-south roads were named after Chinese provinces, and east-west ones named after Chinese cities. The north-south roads include Xizang Road, Henan Road and Guangxi Road; while the east-west ones include Nanjing Road, Fuzhou Road and Yan’an Road. The only exception is east-west Guangdong Road named after Guangdong province. The roads’ names in Chinese are arranged as: province / city name + direction + number + road.
For example, East Zhongshan 1st Road, in Chinese pinyin, is Zhongshan (city name) + Dong (East) + Yi (1st) + Lu (Road).
The followings are Shanghai layout guide about roads in Chinese pinyin and English:

I am trying to call my husband in Shanghai on a Chinese cellphone he has been given there. The number is 352-424-9460, so I am dialing 011863524249460 from the US. It never rings (I get a fast busy). Are you sure that this is cell phone number? However, in China, the cell phone number is made up of 11 numbers. Obviously, another number is left out. I guess it should be '1'. Hello, the Shanghai zip code is right but you have a wrong spelling, that is nanjing west road not nanging.

I have a friend in Shanghai. Trying to contact a friend. How to dial/call Shanghai from Australia/UK/USA?

Here are 4 steps:

3. Add the Shanghai area code ‘021’ from Australia/UK/USA

240-hour Visa-free Transit in Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu
 From Dec. 17, 2024, the duration of 144h visa-free transit policy has been extended to 240h for tourism, family visits, exchange visits and business. More importantly, travelers can now cross provincial boundaries to travel between the permitted 24 provinces, regions and municipalities which cover most tourist cities across Mainland China through 60 ports.  See the province and port list on 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit
Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang has adopted the 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit, which targets citizens from 54 countries and regions and allows them to transit in 24 provinces and regions of Mainland China including Shanghai, Jiangsu and Zhejiang for a stay length not more than 240 hours, ie., 10 days.
Who can enjoy the 240-hour visa-free transit in Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang? - List of 54 Qualified Countries
 25 Schengen Agreement Countries: Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland
 15 Other European Countries: Russia, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Cyprus, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Montenegro, Macedonia (FYROM), Albania, Belarus, Monaco
 6 American Countries: the United States, Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Chile
 2 Oceania Countries: Australia, New Zealand
 6 Asian Countries: Korea, Japan, Singapore, Brunei, United Arab Emirates, Qatar
Things to Know before Designing Your Visa-free Travel Plan
 No. 1: Transit Route: Country A → 24 Provinces of China → Country B
Visitors applying for the 240-hour visa-free transit need to hold a ticket to a third country or region. Notably, passengers can have multiple stopovers in all the 24 provinces no exceeding 240 hours in total. In this context, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan are considered as third regions, which is a great help for planning a transiting route. For example, if a visitor coming from the UK wants to use the visa-free transit but actually have no plan to another country after visiting Shanghai, he or she can leave for Hong Kong, and then go back home.
 Eg: √  UK – Shanghai - Guangzhou- Hong Kong
 see the 24 provinces and eligible port list on China 240-Hour Visa-Free Policy
 No. 2: The actual allowed stay length is calculated from 00:00 after the date of your entry, therefore you can maximize your stay by taking an early flight on the date of entry and a late flight on the date of exit.
 No. 3: Some passengers may try to cancel the ticket to the third country or region after arrival and book a ticket back to the departure country instead, while this is not allowed within the visa-free policy. Don't risk doing this for you may face serious results.
Areas Allowed to Stay
Passengers eligible for the 240-hour visa-free transit can travel within 24 provinces and regions housing most tourist cities in China. 
How to Apply for 240-Hour Visa-Free Transit in Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu
Prepare the required documents, including a passport valid for at least three months from the date of entry, a valid visa to the third country or region if required, and a ticket to the third country or region. Visitors had better also prepare hotel bookings in case of immigration check. Then follow the steps in the chart.  Good News: Passengers wishing to use 240-hour visa-free transit in Shanghai can log into the online platform (https://gaj.sh.gov.cn/crj/144zy.jsp) to make the application in advance. The system will pop up notices if you do not qualify for the visa-free transit policy, reducing the risks of being denied on the spot. After arrival, you can use the self-help machine to print the Arrival Card.
What Are the Eligible Transit Ports?
According to the rules, all ports in Shanghai, Nanjing Lukou Airport, Ningbo Lishe Airport and Hangzhou Xiaoshan Airport are the eligible ports for the 240-hour visa-free transit scheme. Eligible Ports Contact Information Shanghai Pudong Airport 0086-21-96990 Hongqiao Airport 0086-21-96990 Shanghai Railway Station 0086-21-12306 Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal 0086-21-66593501 Shanghai Port International Cruise Terminal 0086-21-51105100 Jiangsu Nanjing Lukou Airport 0086-25-968890 Port of Lianyungang 0086-400-0518-999  Zhejiang Hangzhou Xiaoshan Airport 0086-571-96299 Ningbo Lishe Airport 0086-574-81899000 Wenzhou International Cruise Port -- Zhoushan International Cruise Port 0086-0580-2181681 
Note: Currently, train passengers can only get in / out through Shanghai Railway Station, which operates trains to and from Kowloon, Hong Kong every other day.
What Can I Do During the 240 Hours in Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang?
Taste the flavor of old and modern Shanghai
Shanghai, as an open port city, is where the east and west meet. Spending one or two days in the city, you can visit Shikumen, a unique residence style, to find the traces of old Shanghai in the narrow alleys. In Lujiazui, dense high rises present the thriving and energetic side of Shanghai. Choose one from Shanghai Tower, the World Financial Center, and the Oriental Pearl Tower to overlook the city and you will never regret. If travelling with your kids, set aside one more day for Shanghai Disneyland Park to enrich your trip.
Take a side trip to nearby cities by bullet train
During the 240-hour visa-free period, no matter you are transiting in Nanjing, Hangzhou, or Shanghai, you can include nearby cities in your itinerary by high speed train. Usually, it takes less than two hours to travel between. Different from Shanghai, Jiangsu and Zhejiang are more classical and characterized by the water towns. A side trip to water towns like Wuzhen, Xitang near Hangzhou and Tongli, Zhouzhuang near Suzhou can highlight your trip.
Enjoy night activities
Night activities in Shanghai are colorful. You can take a cruise on the Huangpu River to enjoy the night scene along the banks or wander around the Nanjing Road to experience the local life. When travelling in Suzhou, the unique story-telling ballad and Kun Opera performed in classical gardens at night are a feast for your ears.
